items.title: Unit, time and spectral correspondence between the physical scattering operators and the nondimensional Laplacian
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $m,\hbar>0$, put
$c:=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b) in dimension $d=3$, let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ be measurable
and put $W:=V/c$. For a measurable $U$ let $M_U$ be the maximal
multiplication operator on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$, with
$D(M_U):=\{f\in L^2:Uf\in L^2\}$ and $M_Uf:=Uf$. Write
$$A_{0}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{4\pi^{2}|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(A_{0}):=\bigl\{f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C):|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\bigr\},$$
$$A:=A_{0}+M_{W},\quad D(A):=D(A_{0}),\qquad H_{0}:=cA_{0},\qquad H:=cA=cA_{0}+M_{V}.$$
$D(A_{0})\subseteq D(M_V)=D(M_W)$ is assumed, and assume that
$A=A_0+M_W$ is self-adjoint on $D(A_0)$. These two hypotheses hold
automatically for real bounded measurable $V$ by
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a),(c), so every original bounded-potential case is retained.
So $A_{0}$ is the operator $-\Delta_{w}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] and
$D(A_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]). For a self-adjoint operator $T$ write
$E_{T}$ for the regular projection valued measure of
[[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]] and
$\mu^{T}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{T}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ for $\psi\in L^{2}$. Then:

(a) $A$ and $H$ are self-adjoint with domain $D(A)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
and $H=cA$ and $H_{0}=cA_{0}$ hold as operator identities on that common domain;

(b) for every Borel set $B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B),\qquad E_{H_{0}}(cB)=E_{A_{0}}(B);$$
consequently $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(cB)=\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)$ for every $\psi$ and every
Borel $B$, and $\sigma(H)=c\,\sigma(A)$, $\sigma(H_{0})=c\,\sigma(A_{0})$;

(c) for every $t\in\mathbb R$, with $\tau:=\hbar t/(2m)=\frac{tc}{\hbar}$,
$$e^{-itH/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A},\qquad e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A_{0}},$$
where the exponentials are those of
[[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]];

(d) let $F:\mathbb R\to\mathcal B(L^{2})$ be any family of bounded operators and
$\tau(t):=\hbar t/(2m)$. For every $\psi\in L^{2}$ the strong limit
$\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}F(\tau(t))\psi$ exists if and only if
$\lim_{\tau\to\pm\infty}F(\tau)\psi$ exists, and then the two limits are equal;
in particular
$$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar} =\operatorname*{s-lim}_{\tau\to\pm\infty}e^{i\tau A}e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$$
in the sense that either strong limit exists exactly when the other does, and
then they are equal;

(e) $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure
if and only if $\mu^{A}_{\psi}$ is, and likewise for singularity with respect
to Lebesgue measure and for absence of atoms; and $\psi\ne0$ is an eigenvector
of $H$ with eigenvalue $\lambda$ if and only if it is an eigenvector of $A$
with eigenvalue $\lambda/c$.

The statement is an operator identity and a statement about spectral measures;
no physical interpretation, no scattering limit and no cross section is
asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the parameters $m,\hbar>0$ and $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$; the real measurable $V$ and $W=V/c$, with $D(A_0)\subseteq D(M_V)$ and $A=A_0+M_W$ self-adjoint on $D(A_0)$; the operators $A_{0},A,H_{0},H$ of the statement; the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **The free operator and its Sobolev domain.** With $\mathcal F_{2}$ as above and $c_{0}:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, the operator $\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c_{0}|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2}$ on $\{f:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in L^{2}\}$ is self-adjoint, its domain is $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and it acts as $f\mapsto-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f$ ([[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] clause (a), [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]).

[F2] **Free plus bounded potential.** For $d\ge1$, $c_{0}>0$, $b\in\mathbb R$ and real measurable bounded $V_{0}$, the operator $\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c_{0}|\xi|^{2}+b}\mathcal F_{2}$ is self-adjoint on its stated domain, and $H:=H_{0}+M_{V_{0}}$ is self-adjoint on $D(H_{0})$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F3] **Positive scaling of self-adjoint operators.** For $c_{0}>0$ and a densely defined self-adjoint $A$ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, the operator $c_{0}A$ with domain $D(A)$ is self-adjoint, $\rho(c_{0}A)=c_{0}\rho(A)$ and $\sigma(c_{0}A)=c_{0}\sigma(A)$ ([[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F4] **The spectral theorem.** Every self-adjoint operator $T$ on a nonzero complex Hilbert space has a unique regular projection valued measure $E_{T}$ on the Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R$ with $D(T)=\{x:\int\lambda^{2}dE_{T,x}(\lambda)<\infty\}$ and $Tx=\int\lambda\,dE_{T}(\lambda)x$ for $x\in D(T)$; conversely, for a regular projection valued measure $F$ the operator $\int\lambda\,dF$ with that domain is self-adjoint with projection valued measure $F$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F5] **Bounded and unbounded projection valued integrals.** For a bounded measurable $g$ the operator $\Phi_{E}(g)$ satisfies $\langle\Phi_{E}(g)x,y\rangle=\int g\,dE_{x,y}$ and $\|\Phi_{E}(g)\|\le\|g\|_{\infty}$ ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clauses 1, 2); for measurable $f$ the operator $f(E)$ has domain $D(f(E))=\{x:\int|f|^{2}dE_{x}<\infty\}$ and is the norm limit of the bounded integrals of the truncations $f\mathbf 1_{\{|f|\le n\}}$ ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]). The same bounded integral also satisfies $\|\Phi_E(g)x\|^2=\int|g|^2dE_x$; bounded measurable $g_n$ with $|g_n|\le C|f|$ and $g_n\to f$ pointwise satisfy $g_n(E)x\to f(E)x$ for $x\in D(f(E))$ ([[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]], final clause).

[F6] **The exponential as a projection valued integral.** For self-adjoint $T$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, $e^{itT}=\int e^{it\lambda}\,dE_{T}(\lambda)$ is a strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group with generator $iT$ ([[lem-self-adjoint-operator-generates-a-strongly-continuous-unitary-group]]); this is the bounded functional calculus of [[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] applied to the bounded continuous functions $\lambda\mapsto e^{it\lambda}$.

[F7] **Scalar convergence and Lebesgue scaling.** If $0\le f_n\uparrow f$ pointwise for measurable functions, $\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu$ ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]]). For $c>0$ on $\mathbb R$, dilation preserves Lebesgue measurability and $\lambda(cB)=c\lambda(B)$, hence it and its inverse preserve null sets ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-under-dilations-and-reflections]] clauses (2),(3), with $n=1$).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the two operators on their common domain, push the projection valued measure forward along $\lambda\mapsto c\lambda$ and use the uniqueness clause of the spectral theorem, then transfer the exponential and the strong limits by the change of variables $\tau=\hbar t/(2m)$.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F7].

1.1 Applying [F1] with $m=1/2$, $\hbar=1$ gives $c_{0}=4\pi^{2}$ and shows that $A_{0}=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{4\pi^{2}|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2}$ is self-adjoint with $D(A_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and $A_{0}f=-\Delta_{w}f$. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Multiplying by $c>0$, [F3] clause (a) makes $cA_0=H_0$ self-adjoint on $D(A_0)$, and [F1] identifies its action with $-\hbar^2\Delta_w/(2m)$. Since $W=V/c$ and $c\ne0$, the maximal multiplier domains satisfy $D(M_W)=D(M_V)$; the assumed inclusion $D(A_0)\subseteq D(M_V)$ makes both sums well defined on the common domain. The operator $A=A_0+M_W$ is self-adjoint there by hypothesis, and [F3] makes $H=cA$ self-adjoint on that same domain. For $f\in D(A_0)$, $cAf=cA_0f+cWf=cA_0f+Vf$, proving (a). If $V$ is bounded, $M_V$ is bounded on all $L^2$ and [F2] proves the assumed self-adjointness of $A$ automatically; this retains the original branch. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

1.3 Put $m_c(\lambda)=c\lambda$ and, for Borel $B$, $F(B):=E_A(m_c^{-1}(B))=E_A(B/c)$. Preimages preserve intersections and countable disjoint unions, so [F4] gives the projection, identity and strong countable-additivity axioms for $F$. For every $x$, $F_x(B)=E_{A,x}(B/c)$. This scalar measure is regular: a compact $K\subseteq B/c$ approximating $E_{A,x}(B/c)$ transports to the compact $cK\subseteq B$ with the same measure, and an open $U\supseteq B/c$ with arbitrarily small excess transports to the open $cU\supseteq B$ with the same excess. These follow from regularity of $E_{A,x}$ and the homeomorphism $m_c$. Thus $F$ is a regular PVM, with the preimage direction appropriate to scaling $A$ by $c$. [F4, algebra]

1.4 Let $\psi,y\in L^{2}$. If $\lim_{\tau\to+\infty}F(\tau)\psi=y$, then for $\epsilon>0$ there is $S$ with $\|F(\tau)\psi-y\|<\epsilon$ for $\tau>S$; since $\tau(t)=\hbar t/(2m)\to+\infty$ as $t\to+\infty$, there is $T$ with $\tau(t)>S$ for $t>T$, so $\|F(\tau(t))\psi-y\|<\epsilon$ for $t>T$. Conversely, if $\lim_{t\to+\infty}F(\tau(t))\psi=y$, let $\epsilon>0$ and $T$ with $\|F(\tau(t))\psi-y\|<\epsilon$ for $t>T$; for $\tau>\tau(T)$ the inverse $\tau\mapsto2m\tau/\hbar$ gives $t(\tau)>T$, so $\|F(\tau)\psi-y\|<\epsilon$. The case $t,\tau\to-\infty$ is identical with reversed inequalities. [given, algebra]

2.1 For a complex simple function $g=\sum_k a_k\mathbf1_{B_k}$, $\Phi_F(g)=\sum_k a_kE_A(B_k/c)=\Phi_{E_A}(g\circ m_c)$, since $\mathbf1_{B_k/c}(\lambda)=\mathbf1_{B_k}(c\lambda)$. For bounded Borel $g$, choose simple $g_n$ uniformly approaching $g$; then $g_n\circ m_c$ approaches $g\circ m_c$ uniformly, and [F5] gives $\Phi_F(g)=\Phi_{E_A}(g\circ m_c)$ by operator-norm limits. In particular $\|\Phi_F(g)x\|^2=\int|g|^2dF_x=\int|g(c\lambda)|^2dE_{A,x}(\lambda)$ for every $x$. [F5, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 Let $g_n(\lambda):=\lambda\mathbf1_{\{|\lambda|\le n\}}$. Step 2.1 gives $\Phi_F(g_n)=\Phi_{E_A}\bigl(c\lambda\mathbf1_{\{|c\lambda|\le n\}}\bigr)$; the cutoff is $|c\lambda|\le n$, not $|\lambda|\le n$. Its squared-norm identity and [F7] applied to the increasing squared cutoffs give $\int\lambda^2dF_x=c^2\int\lambda^2dE_{A,x}$, including possibly infinite values, for every $x$. Thus the identity-integral domain for $F$ is exactly $D(A)$ by [F4], [F5]. On that domain, the bounded functions $k_n(\lambda):=\lambda\mathbf1_{\{|c\lambda|\le n\}}$ approach $\lambda$ pointwise and satisfy $|k_n|\le|\lambda|$, so the actual cutoff-convergence clause of [F5] gives $\Phi_{E_A}(k_n)x\to Ax$. Therefore $\int\lambda\,dF\,x=\lim_n\Phi_F(g_n)x=c\lim_n\Phi_{E_A}(k_n)x=cAx$. The domain and action both match $cA$. [F4, F5, F7, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By steps 1.3 and 3.1, the identity integral of the regular PVM $F$ equals $cA=H$ on exactly $D(A)$. The converse and uniqueness clauses of [F4] therefore give $E_H=F$, namely $E_H(B)=E_A(B/c)$, equivalently $E_H(cB)=E_A(B)$. Running the same argument for the self-adjoint free operator $A_0$ gives $E_{H_0}(cB)=E_{A_0}(B)$. Scalar pairings yield $\mu^H_\psi(cB)=\mu^A_\psi(B)$, and [F3] clause (b) gives $\sigma(H)=c\sigma(A)$ and $\sigma(H_0)=c\sigma(A_0)$, proving (b). [F4, F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By [F7], $m_c$ and its inverse preserve Lebesgue null sets. Step 4.1 transports each scalar measure by this bijection, so a measure vanishes on every null set exactly when its counterpart does; a measure supported on a null set transports to one supported on the scaled null set, and conversely. Point masses satisfy $\mu^H_\psi(\{\lambda\})=\mu^A_\psi(\{\lambda/c\})$, so absence of atoms is preserved as well. On the common domain, $H\psi=cA\psi$ makes $H\psi=\lambda\psi$ equivalent to $A\psi=(\lambda/c)\psi$ for $\psi\ne0$, proving (e). [F7, step 1.2, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 For $t\in\mathbb R$ put $\tau=\hbar t/(2m)$, so that $t\lambda/\hbar=\tau\mu$ with $\lambda=c\mu$; by [F6] and the bounded case of 2.1 applied to the bounded measurable function $g(\lambda)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau\lambda/c}$ one has $e^{-itH/\hbar}=\int e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\,dE_{H}(\lambda)=\int e^{-i\tau\mu}\,dE_{A}(\mu)=e^{-i\tau A}$, and the same identity with $H_{0},A_{0}$ gives the second display of (c). [F6, step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 With $F(\tau):=e^{i\tau A}e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$ and $G(t):=e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH_{0}/\hbar}$, step 5.2 gives $G(t)=F(\tau(t))$ for every $t$; so step 1.4 shows that the strong limits $\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}G(t)$ and $\operatorname*{s-lim}_{\tau\to\pm\infty}F(\tau)$ exist exactly together and then coincide. This is (d) and completes the proof. [step 5.2, step 1.4, given] ∎

## Remarks

- **Use.** The lemma is the exact bookkeeping that transfers every statement
  proved for the nondimensional operators $-\Delta+M_{W}$ and their free wave
  operators into the physical operators $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta+M_{V}$
  and their physical-time wave operators, and it carries the free spectral
  density along the energy rescaling $E=c\lambda$. It asserts nothing about
  the existence of the wave operators themselves; that is the content of the
  scattering existence theorem of the pair.
- **Choice.** The spectral theorem and the projection valued integrals used
  here carry the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice; no further
  choice principle is used.

items.title: The three-dimensional continuity identity, the vanishing stationary divergence and the incident and outgoing current readings
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$m,\hbar>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^{3}$ and $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be
nonempty open sets ([[def-interval]]), and let
$u,v:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$ be functions of class $C^{2}$
([[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]) that satisfy the two real
equations
$$\hbar\,\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv,\qquad -\hbar\,\partial_{t}v=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu$$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$ for a real-valued function $V$ on $\Omega\times
I$, where $\Delta=\partial_{1}^{2}+\partial_{2}^{2}+\partial_{3}^{2}$
([[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]) and where the equations are the
componentwise reading of
$i\hbar\,\partial_{t}\psi=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\psi+V\psi$ for
$\psi:=u+iv$. Put
$$n:=u^{2}+v^{2}:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R,\qquad \mathbf j:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\bigl(u\,\nabla v-v\,\nabla u\bigr):\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^{3},$$
with $\nabla$ the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and
$\operatorname{div}$ the divergence of
[[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. Then:

(a) *Continuity identity.* $\partial_{t}n+\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$
pointwise on $\Omega\times I$.

(b) *Stationary solutions.* If $u,v:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ are $C^{2}$ and
independent of $t$, if $V:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ is real, and if there is a real
$E$ with
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu=Eu,\qquad -\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv=Ev$$
pointwise on $\Omega$, then $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$ on $\Omega$ for the
time-independent field $\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\nabla v-v\nabla u)$, and for
every closed ball $\overline{B(a,r)}\subseteq\Omega$ with outward unit normal
$\nu$ on the sphere $\partial B(a,r)$,
$$\int_{\partial B(a,r)}\mathbf j\cdot\nu\,dS=0 .$$

(c) *The two explicit readings.* Let $k>0$, $d\in S^{2}$ and define
$u(x):=\cos(kd\cdot x)$, $v(x):=\sin(kd\cdot x)$ on $\Omega=\mathbb R^{3}$
(then $u,v$ are $C^{\infty}$ and satisfy the stationary equations with $V=0$,
$E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$). Then
$$\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\,d\qquad\text{on }\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Let $r_{0}>0$, write $\Omega:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{3}:|x|>r_{0}\}$, let
$\Omega\ni x=r\,\omega$ with $r=|x|$, $\omega\in S^{2}$, and let
$a,b:S^{2}\to\mathbb R$ be functions with $a,b\in C^{1}$; define
$$u(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\cos(kr)-b(\omega)\sin(kr)}{r},\qquad v(x):=\frac{a(\omega)\sin(kr)+b(\omega)\cos(kr)}{r}$$
on $\Omega$, so that $u+iv=\frac{f(\omega)}{r}e^{ikr}$ with $f:=a+ib$. Then
$u,v\in C^{1}(\Omega)$ and, with $\hat r:=\omega$,
$$\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f(\omega)|^{2}}{r^{2}},\qquad \text{equivalently}\qquad r^{2}\,\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar k}{m}|f(\omega)|^{2},$$
and the current identity holds for every declared $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$, with no
equation required of the field.

The assertion is an identity for the declared differentiable functions; it
constructs no probability law, no state, no beam and no cross section. The
fields of clause (c) are only $C^{1}$: an $f\in C^{1}(S^{2})$ need not admit
two angular derivatives, and no outgoing field is claimed here to solve the
free equation or to be stationary.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the open sets $\Omega,I$, the functions $u,v,V$, the constants $m,\hbar>0$, and the data of clause (c).

[F1] **Differentiation rules.** For totally differentiable Euclidean maps the sum and scalar-multiple rules hold ([[thm-algebra-of-total-derivatives]]) and the chain rule $D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a)$ holds ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]), with $Df(a)e_{j}=\partial_{j}f(a)$ recovering the partial derivatives ([[thm-total-derivative-computes-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]); the partial derivatives themselves are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], the entries of the Jacobian of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. For scalar functions on an interval the sum, product and quotient rules hold ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), and $(\sin)'=\cos$ and $(\cos)'=-\sin$ on $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]).

[F2] **Divergence of a product with a scalar.** For $C^{1}$ functions $\varphi:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ and $F:\Omega\to\mathbb R^{3}$, the equality $\operatorname{div}(\varphi F)=\langle\nabla\varphi,F\rangle+\varphi\operatorname{div}F$ holds pointwise, the divergence and gradient being those of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] ([[lem-divergence-and-curl-are-linear-and-obey-the-scalar-product-rules]]).

[F3] **Divergence theorem.** Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$. For a bounded $C^{1}$ domain $\Omega_{0}$ and $F\in C^{1}(\overline{\Omega_{0}};\mathbb R^{3})$, $\int_{\Omega_{0}}\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega_{0}}F\cdot\nu\,dS$ ([[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; differentiate $n$, use the two real equations to cancel the terms, then evaluate the stationary divergence and the two explicit fields.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 By [F1], $\partial_{t}n=\partial_{t}(u^{2}+v^{2})=2(u\,\partial_{t}u+v\,\partial_{t}v)$ pointwise on $\Omega\times I$. [F1, given]

1.2 Put $F:=u\nabla v-v\nabla u$. By [F2] applied to each of the two products, using $\operatorname{div}(\nabla v)=\sum_{i}\partial_{i}\partial_{i}v=\Delta v$ and likewise for $u$, one has $\operatorname{div}(u\nabla v)=\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+u\,\Delta v$ and $\operatorname{div}(v\nabla u)=\nabla v\cdot\nabla u+v\,\Delta u$; the mixed terms are equal by symmetry of the inner product and cancel in the difference, so $\operatorname{div}F=u\,\Delta v-v\,\Delta u$ and hence $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\Delta v-v\Delta u)$. [F2, F1, algebra]

1.3 Reading the complex equation $i\hbar\partial_{t}(u+iv)=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta(u+iv)+V(u+iv)$ by real and imaginary parts gives $\hbar\,\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta v+Vv$ and $-\hbar\,\partial_{t}v=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta u+Vu$, i.e. $\partial_{t}u=-\frac{\hbar}{2m}\Delta v+\frac{V}{\hbar}v$ and $\partial_{t}v=\frac{\hbar}{2m}\Delta u-\frac{V}{\hbar}u$. [given, algebra]

1.4 For $u=\cos(kd\cdot x)$, $v=\sin(kd\cdot x)$ the chain rule [F1] gives $\nabla u=-k\,d\,\sin(kd\cdot x)$ and $\nabla v=k\,d\,\cos(kd\cdot x)$; hence $u\nabla v-v\nabla u=k\,d\,(\cos^{2}+\sin^{2})=k\,d$ and $\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar k}{m}d$. The two functions are $C^{\infty}$ and satisfy the stationary equations with $V=0$, because $\partial_{i}\partial_{i}u=-k^{2}d_{i}^{2}\cos(kd\cdot x)$ and $\partial_{i}\partial_{i}v=-k^{2}d_{i}^{2}\sin(kd\cdot x)$ by [F1], so summing over $i$ and using $|d|^{2}=1$ gives $\Delta u=-k^{2}u$ and $\Delta v=-k^{2}v$ with $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$. [F1, given, algebra]

1.5 Write $c_{k}:=\cos(kr)$, $s_{k}:=\sin(kr)$ and $f=a+ib$. Then $u=r^{-1}(ac_{k}-bs_{k})$, $v=r^{-1}(as_{k}+bc_{k})$, so by the chain and product rules for functions of the single variable $r$ [F1], $\partial_{r}u=-k\,r^{-1}(as_{k}+bc_{k})-r^{-2}(ac_{k}-bs_{k})$ and $\partial_{r}v=k\,r^{-1}(ac_{k}-bs_{k})-r^{-2}(as_{k}+bc_{k})$. Multiplying out, $u\,\partial_{r}v-v\,\partial_{r}u=k\,r^{-2}\bigl[(ac_{k}-bs_{k})^{2}+(as_{k}+bc_{k})^{2}\bigr]=k\,r^{-2}(a^{2}+b^{2})=k\,r^{-2}|f(\omega)|^{2}$; since $\hat r$ is a unit vector and the radial directional derivative of an angular function is zero, $\mathbf j\cdot\hat r=\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\,\partial_{r}v-v\,\partial_{r}u)$, which is the first display of (c), and multiplying by $r^{2}>0$ gives the equivalent second display. Both $u$ and $v$ are $C^{1}$ on $\Omega$: they are sums of products of the $C^{\infty}$ radial factors $r^{-1}$, $\cos(kr)$, $\sin(kr)$ with the $C^{1}$ angular factors $a,b$, and the chain rule [F1] applied in the angular directions gives the stated regularity. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 Substituting 1.3 into 1.1 and using that $V$ is real, $2(u\partial_{t}u+v\partial_{t}v)=2\bigl(-\frac{\hbar}{2m}u\Delta v+\frac{V}{\hbar}uv+\frac{\hbar}{2m}v\Delta u-\frac{V}{\hbar}vu\bigr)=-\frac{\hbar}{m}(u\Delta v-v\Delta u)$. Adding the value of $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j$ from 1.2 gives $\partial_{t}n+\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=0$, which is (a). [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, algebra]

2.2 If $u,v,V$ do not depend on $t$ and satisfy the stationary equations, then $\Delta u=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}(V-E)u$ and $\Delta v=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}(V-E)v$ pointwise, so 1.2 gives $\operatorname{div}\mathbf j=\frac{\hbar}{m}\cdot\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}(V-E)(uv-vu)=0$ on $\Omega$. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 Let $\overline{B(a,r)}\subseteq\Omega$. The ball $B(a,r)$ is a bounded $C^{1}$ domain and $\mathbf j$ is $C^{1}$ on a neighbourhood of its closure, so [F3] gives $\int_{\partial B(a,r)}\mathbf j\cdot\nu\,dS=\int_{B(a,r)}\operatorname{div}\mathbf j\,dx=0$ by 2.2; with 1.4 for the plane-wave reading, 1.5 for the outgoing current identity, 2.1 for (a) and this step for (b), the proof of (a), (b) and (c) is complete. [F3, step 1.4, step 1.5, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Role.** The lemma supplies the exact current reading used by the pair's
  stationary beam model: $\mathbf j$ is the pair of clauses (a) and (b) that
  makes the current of a stationary solution divergence-free and flux-free
  through spheres, and clause (c) computes the two currents -- the incident
  plane wave with magnitude $\hbar k/m$ and the outgoing spherical wave with
  radial density $(\hbar k/m)|f|^{2}/r^{2}$ -- that the model's cross-section
  reading compares. Clause (c) asserts the outgoing current identity without
  any equation for the field: the model's amplitude $f_{k}$ appears in the
  outgoing coefficient of the full stationary solution (incident wave plus
  outgoing wave plus remainder), whose existence and equation are established
  by the pair's stationary theorem, not here.
- **Choice.** The divergence theorem used in 3.1 assumes countable choice; no
  additional choice principle is used.

items.title: The declared short-range scattering model: state space, potential classes, assigned energy observables, asymptotic vocabulary and units
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5, the identical-particle
and spin postulate P6, and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]). Fix a mass parameter
$m>0$ and a spin label $s=0$, so that the framework's one-particle model
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] reads its state space as
$H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with the pairing linear in the first
argument, its componentwise position family $Q_{1},Q_{2},Q_{3}$, its
componentwise momentum family $P_{1},P_{2},P_{3}$ and the action constant
$\hbar>0$; the spin-zero internal factor carries the trivial representation of
P6. Units are those of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: position
is read in metres, momentum in $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, energy and potential
energy in joules, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice as the choice hypotheses of the cited
mathematical suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared scattering model and its potential classes.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **short-range scattering
model**. Its declared state space is $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ of
clause (a), with the position and momentum families of that clause. A
**declared short-range potential** of the model is a real-valued measurable
function $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ satisfying either

1. *(compact-support class)* $V$ is bounded, $\|V\|_{\infty}<\infty$, and
   $V=0$ almost everywhere outside some ball
   $B_{\mathrm{supp}}:=\{x:|x|\le R_{\mathrm{supp}}\}$ with
   $R_{\mathrm{supp}}<\infty$; or
2. *(resolvent-tail class)* $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with real
   $V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and real bounded $V_{\mathrm b}$, and, with
   the reduced potential $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}:=W_{2}+W_{\mathrm b}$ and the
   nondimensional free operator $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ of clause (c) (so that
   $H^{\mathrm{free}}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{0}$), the function
$$h(r):=\bigl\|M_{W}(A_{0}-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\bigr\|, \qquad r\ge0,$$
   is finite for every $r$ and belongs to $L^{1}([0,\infty))$.

The function $V$ is read as a potential energy in joules; the model asserts no
derivation of $V$ from P5 or from any force law, and an assignment of a
concrete target to $V$ is a tested identification in the sense of clause (iii)
of P7 carrying the corresponding uncertainty. The pure Coulomb potential
$V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$, $\kappa>0$, is **not** in either class: it is a declared
long-range model with its own definition and comparison construction
on this page.

**(c) Assigned energy observables.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] its domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]) and
$H^{\mathrm{free}}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f$ with $\Delta_{w}$ the
weak Laplacian ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
Write $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ for this **nondimensional free operator**, so that
$H^{\mathrm{free}}=(\hbar^{2}/2m)A_{0}$ on the common domain, and
$W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}$ for the **reduced potential** of a declared potential $V$.
With $M_V$ the maximal multiplication operator, $D(M_V)=\{f\in L^2:Vf\in L^2\}$ (bounded and everywhere defined in the compact-support class), the **assigned energy observables** of the model with declared
potential $V$ are the free operator $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and the interacting
operator
$$H:=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H):=D(H^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. For the compact-support class,
clause (c) of the cited theorem makes $H$ self-adjoint on $D(H)$ and bounded
below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; for the resolvent-tail class, self-adjointness of
$H$ on the same domain is proved on this page and is not presupposed here. The
model adopts $(H^{\mathrm{free}},\mathrm J)$ and $(H,\mathrm J)$ as assigned
sharp observables in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), and
reads their flows by [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
with $U_{\mathrm{free}}(t)=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ and
$U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$.

**(d) Short-range scattering vocabulary.** For a declared short-range
potential $V$ the model declares the **free asymptotic comparison** to be the
pair of strong limits
$$\Omega_{\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar},$$
which are declared **wave operators** of the model when both limits exist, and
declares the **scattering operator** $S:=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ when both
exist and $\Omega_{\pm}$ are isometries. The model says that the pair is
**asymptotically complete** for this $V$ when the two ranges agree with the
subspace
$$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ll\lambda\},$$
where $\mu^{H}_{\psi}(B):=\langle E_{H}(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ is the scalar
spectral measure of the projection valued measure $E_{H}$ of the self-adjoint
operator $H$, and with
$$H_{\mathrm c}(H):=H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)^{\perp},\qquad H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H):=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\psi\ne0:H\psi=\lambda\psi\ \text{for some }\lambda\in\mathbb R\};$$
here $H_{\mathrm{pp}}(H)$ is the closed linear span of the eigenvectors of $H$.
An **asymptotic free state** of a vector $\psi\in H_{0}$ is a vector
$\psi_{\mathrm{in}}$ such that
$\bigl\|e^{-itH/\hbar}\psi-e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi_{\mathrm{in}}\bigr\|\to0$
as $t\to-\infty$; the model reads this limit relation through the
wave-operator identity $\psi=\Omega_{-}\psi_{\mathrm{in}}$ only when the wave
operator exists. These
are declarations of the model under P4; they construct no preparation,
detector or measured count, and no definition of a cross section appears here.

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(d) fix the data of the pair: a declared
state space, two declared potential classes, two assigned energy observables
with their units, and the wave-operator, scattering-operator and
asymptotic-completeness vocabulary. They introduce no assumption beyond P1,
P2, P4, P5, P6, P7 and the cited mathematics; in particular the potential
classes are declarations, not consequences of the framework, and no
identification of $m$, $\hbar$ or $V$ with measured data is asserted. The
existence of the limits, the completeness of the ranges and every cross
section are separate theorems of the pair.

## Remarks

- **Why two classes.** The compact-support class is the minimal physically
  transparent case in which the pair's completeness theorem is proved; the
  resolvent-tail class is the wider class in which the same conclusion is
  proved from an integrable decay hypothesis on the shifted free resolvent
  tail. The Coulomb potential fails both classes and is treated separately
  by the long-range definition of this page.
- **Names.** The symbols $\Omega_{\pm}$, $S$, $H_{\mathrm{ac}}$, $H_{\mathrm{pp}}$
  and $H_{\mathrm c}$ are declared here once and used with exactly this
  meaning on this page and its companion.

items.title: The declared stationary elastic beam model: incident plane wave, scattered wave, current readings and differential and total cross sections
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
and the preparation and apparatus discipline P7
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]]), with the short-range
scattering model of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]]: mass $m>0$, spin zero,
state space $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, a declared short-range
potential $V$, the free and interacting assigned energy observables
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and $H$, its reading of the flow by
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) Incident plane-wave reading and declared density scale.** As an
additional model assumption of the pair, adopt the **stationary elastic beam
model**. Fix a **wave number** $k>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$, a **direction**
$d\in S^2$, and an **incident number-density scale** $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. This scale is an explicitly declared model normalization;
no numerical sample density or measured beam value is supplied. Retain the
unit-amplitude, dimensionless incident shape
$$u_{\mathrm{inc}}(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x},$$
with energy reading $E:=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$ in joules. The **physical incident
beam field** is $\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\,u_{\mathrm{inc}}$,
with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$ and constant model number density
$|\Phi_{\mathrm{inc}}|^2=n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. For a dimensionless unit-amplitude
shape $\psi$, write $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]:=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$ for the mathematical current of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]. Its incident
value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, with velocity unit $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The model's
**physical number-current density** is the current of
$\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$,
$$\mathbf j[\Phi]:=\frac{\hbar}{m}\operatorname{Im}(\overline\Phi\nabla\Phi)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi].$$
Thus the **incident current density** and **incident flux density** through a
plane normal to $d$ are
$$\mathbf j_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}d,\qquad J_{\mathrm{inc}}:=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\frac{\hbar k}{m}>0,$$
both in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)5. The mathematical
plane-wave current of the cited lemma remains the unit-shape computation;
the density factor supplies the declared physical beam normalization.

**(c) Scattered-wave reading and generalized stationary solution.** For a
declared short-range potential $V$ the model declares a **generalized
stationary solution** at energy $E$ and direction $d$ to be a function
$\Psi:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C$ of class $C^{2}$ on the complement of
$\operatorname{supp}V$ that satisfies
$$-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\Psi+V\Psi=E\Psi$$
pointwise there and has the **outgoing asymptotic reading**
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}e^{ikr}+\mathcal E(x),\qquad x=r\Omega,\ r\to\infty,$$
with a **scattering amplitude** function $f_k:S^2\to\mathbb C$, read in
metres relative to the unit incident shape, and a physical beam field
$\Phi:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$ with unit $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$. The same
constant factor multiplies its incident, outgoing and remainder terms;
$f_k$ remains the amplitude relative to the incident field, in metres.
Here $\Omega:=x/r$ is the **outgoing unit direction**, and the precise decay
of the remainder $\mathcal E$ is fixed by the existence theorem of this page.
The **scattered physical field** is
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}:=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-u_{\mathrm{inc}})$.
The physical scattered radial current density, obtained by applying the
quadratic current formula to this scattered component, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)\qquad(r\to\infty),$$
in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ for the fixed declared density scale. The leading
unit-shape current is clause (c) of
[[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]; the current of
the remainder is controlled by the stationary theorem. The definition uses
the scattered component, with no assumption that incident/scattered
interference in the total field vanishes.
A generalized stationary solution is generally not an element of $H_{0}$; it
is not a preparation of the model, and clause (d) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] does not apply to it. It
is used only through the declared flux quantities computed from it, and every
such use states the idealization.

**(d) Differential and total cross-section readings.** Under the declared
**equal-channel elastic flux assumptions** -- that the incident and outgoing
readings refer to the same elastic channel at the same energy, that the
incident flux density is spatially uniform over the transverse extent of the
target and the outgoing current is read far outside the support of $V$ -- the
model declares the **differential cross section**
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega):=\lim_{r\to\infty}\frac{r^{2}\,j^{\mathrm{sc}}_{r}(r,\Omega)}{J_{\mathrm{inc}}} =|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}$, and the **total cross section**
$$\sigma:=\int_{S^{2}}\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega)\,d\Omega =\int_{S^{2}}|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\Omega,$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$, whenever the displayed limit and integral exist; the
existence and finiteness of both are proved on this page for the declared
classes. The common positive density factor cancels in the ratio,
$r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}\to |f_k|^2$, so the cross sections are
independent of the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}$. This normalization supplies
no relation to the energy outcome law of P2 and no assertion that an $L^2$
preparation realizes either stationary field.

**(e) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(d) are declarations of the pair under
P1, P2, P4 and P7 together with the short-range model; they are an idealized
stationary reading and not a model of an apparatus. The new density scale is
a symbolic normalization parameter of that reading, not a measured sample
value; multiplication by $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}$ does not turn the
stationary shape into an $L^2$ preparation. In particular no beam
source, target density, collimation, detector acceptance, efficiency,
background or counting procedure appears, and the symbols
$d\sigma/d\Omega$ and $\sigma$ denote model quantities computed from the
declared solution. An identification of a measured count cross section with
these quantities requires a separate preparation and detection model and
carries the uncertainty of that identification.

## Remarks

- **Flux, not probability.** The cross-section readings are ratios of current
  densities of the declared physical stationary fields, whose currents are
  $n_{\mathrm{inc}}$ times the unit-shape currents computed in
  [[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]]; they are not
  read as probabilities of detecting a single particle, and no such
  single-particle statement is asserted.
- **Optical theorem and other refinements.** No optical theorem, dispersion
  relation or inelastic extension is declared or used on this pair.

R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Sections 15.1-15.4 printed pages 209-217: the scattering amplitude, the differential cross section and flux normalization

items.physical_scope: The pair's declared stationary elastic beam model for the short-range scattering model: a monochromatic incident plane-wave reading with wave number and direction, the corresponding current density, the scattered outgoing-wave reading, the declared generalized stationary solution, the idealization that the stationary wave is not a state-space element, the small-target/elastic equal-channel flux assumptions under which the differential and total cross sections are read as ratios of currents, and the units of those quantities. The model is an additional assumption of the pair; it asserts no preparation, no beam apparatus, no count rate and no measured cross section, and no single-particle trajectory claim.

items.title: Existence of the model's wave operators, isometry and intertwining, and the purely absolutely continuous free spectrum
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass parameter $m>0$,
spin zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**compact-support class**, so that $V$ is real, bounded and vanishes almost
everywhere outside a ball $B_{R}$; let $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and
$H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ be the assigned energy observables of the model on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, and let $\Omega_{\pm}$, $S$,
$\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ and $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ be as in clause (d) of that
definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ and bounded
below, and for every Schwartz function $\psi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]])
$$\int_{0}^{\infty}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty, \qquad \int_{-\infty}^{0}\bigl\|Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\bigr\|_{2}\,dt<\infty;$$

(b) the strong limits
$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries of $H_{0}$, so $\Omega_{\pm}^{*}\Omega_{\pm}=I$;
they intertwine the two flows,
$$e^{-isH/\hbar}\Omega_{\pm}=\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\qquad(s\in\mathbb R),$$
and satisfy $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H^{\mathrm{free}}\psi$ for every
$\psi\in D(H^{\mathrm{free}})$;

(c) the free operator has purely absolutely continuous spectrum: for every
$\psi\in H_{0}$ the scalar measure $\mu^{H^{\mathrm{free}}}_{\psi}$ is
absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure and gives zero mass to
$\{0\}$ and to $(-\infty,0)$; hence
$H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{\mathrm c}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{0}$
and $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ has no eigenvalues;

(d) $H$ has no eigenvalue in $(0,\infty)$: if $\psi\in D(H)$, $\psi\ne0$ and
$H\psi=\lambda\psi$ with $\lambda>0$, then no such $\psi$ exists.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics.
It asserts no completeness of the ranges, no unitarity of $S$, no cross
section and no measured quantity; completeness is the content of the two
following theorems of this page.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared short-range scattering model with $m,\hbar>0$, spin zero and a compact-support-class potential $V$ with support in $B_{R}$; the operators $H^{\mathrm{free}}$, $H$ on $W^{2,2}$; the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Scaling correspondence.** With $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ and $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}$, the operators $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ and $A:=-\Delta_{w}+M_{W}$ on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ satisfy $H^{\mathrm{free}}=cA_{0}$ and $H=cA$ on that domain, $E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B)$ for every Borel $B$, $e^{-itH/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A}$ and $e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-i\tau A_{0}}$ with $\tau=\hbar t/(2m)$, the strong limits in the physical and nondimensional times coincide, and $H$ has an eigenvalue $\lambda>0$ if and only if $A$ has the eigenvalue $\lambda/c>0$ ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), (e)).

[F2] **Concrete Cook existence.** Assume Countable Choice. For real $V_{0}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$, with $H_{0}=-\Delta$ on $W^{2,2}$ and $H=H_{0}+M_{V_{0}}$ self-adjoint on the same domain, the Cook integrals $\int_{0}^{\infty}\|V_{0}e^{-itH_{0}}\psi\|_{2}dt$ and its negative-time analogue converge for every Schwartz $\psi$, the wave operators $\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH}e^{-itH_{0}}$ exist as bounded linear isometries with $\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH_{0}}=e^{-isH}\Omega_{\pm}$ and $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H_{0}\psi$ for $\psi\in D(H_{0})$, and $H_{0}$ has purely absolutely continuous spectrum with $L^{2}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{0})$, the scalar spectral measure of $\psi$ having the displayed density with respect to Lebesgue measure and zero mass at $0$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-concrete-three-dimensional-cook-existence]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F3] **Cook isometry and intertwining.** Under the hypotheses of [F2] the wave operators satisfy $\Omega_{\pm}^{*}\Omega_{\pm}=I$, the intertwining identity, and $\Omega_{\pm}D(H_{0})\subseteq D(H)$ with $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H_{0}\psi$; no surjectivity is asserted ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-cook-isometry-and-intertwining]] clauses (a)-(d)).

[F4] **No positive compact-potential eigenvalues.** Assume Countable Choice. For real bounded compactly supported $V_{0}$ and $k>0$, the operator $-\Delta+M_{V_{0}}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ has no eigenvalue $k^{2}$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-no-positive-compact-potential-eigenvalues]]).

[F5] **The model's readings.** The assigned energy observables are $(H^{\mathrm{free}},\mathrm J)$ and $(H,\mathrm J)$ on $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with flow $U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$; in the compact-support class $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)$ and bounded below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$, and the wave operators and the scattering operator are read as the strong limits of the model's flow comparison ([[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clauses (c), (d)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; identify the model's operators with the nondimensional operators of the cited mathematics through the scaling lemma, transfer the Cook estimates by the linear change of variables $\tau=\hbar t/(2m)$, and transfer the spectral statements by the projection valued measure correspondence.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 By [F5], the model supplies self-adjointness of $H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_V$ on $W^{2,2}$ and its lower bound $-\|V\|_\infty$. By [F1], the reduced operator $A=-\Delta_w+M_W$ is self-adjoint on the same domain and $H=cA$, with $W=2mV/\hbar^2$. Since $V$ is real, bounded and compactly supported, so is $W$, and in particular $W\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)$. Thus [F2] applies to the actual reduced potential $V_0=W$ and this already self-adjoint $A$; Cook existence is not used as a proof of the self-adjointness it presupposes. [F1, F2, F5, given]

1.2 For $\psi\in\mathcal S$ put $\tau(t)=\hbar t/(2m)$. By [F1], $Ve^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi=cW e^{-i\tau(t)A_{0}}\psi$, and by [F2] the function $\tau\mapsto\|We^{-i\tau A_{0}}\psi\|_{2}$ is integrable on $[0,\infty)$; the substitution $t\mapsto\tau(t)$ in the Lebesgue integral of a continuous integrand, [[cor-one-dimensional-change-of-variables-with-absolute-derivative]], gives $\int_{0}^{\infty}\|We^{-i\tau(t)A_{0}}\psi\|_{2}dt=\frac{2m}{\hbar}\int_{0}^{\infty}\|We^{-i\tau A_{0}}\psi\|_{2}d\tau<\infty$, hence the first Cook integral of (a); the negative half-line is identical. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.3 By [F1] the strong limits in physical time exist exactly when the nondimensional limits in [F2] exist and then coincide; [F2] exhibits them, so $\Omega_{\pm}$ of the statement exist as strong limits and are the operators of [F2]. This is (b)'s existence assertion. [F2, F1, given]

1.4 Let $\psi\in D(H)$ with $H\psi=\lambda\psi$ and $\lambda>0$. By [F1] $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $A$ with eigenvalue $\lambda/c>0$; [F4] applied with $k=\sqrt{\lambda/c}>0$ gives $\psi=0$. This is (d). [F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 By [F3] the operators of step 1.3 satisfy $\Omega_{\pm}^{*}\Omega_{\pm}=I$, $e^{-isH/\hbar}\Omega_{\pm}=\Omega_{\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ (after replacing the nondimensional time by the physical time through the same reparametrisation) and $H\Omega_{\pm}\psi=\Omega_{\pm}H^{\mathrm{free}}\psi$ for $\psi\in D(H^{\mathrm{free}})$. This completes (b). [F3, step 1.3, algebra]

3.1 By [F2] the scalar measures $\mu^{A_{0}}_{\psi}$ are absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with zero mass at $0$; by [F1] $\mu^{H^{\mathrm{free}}}_{\psi}(B)=\mu^{A_{0}}_{\psi}(c^{-1}B)$, and since multiplication by $c^{-1}>0$ preserves Lebesgue null sets, the transfer preserves absolute continuity and atomlessness, and $\mu^{H^{\mathrm{free}}}_{\psi}(\{0\})=\mu^{A_{0}}_{\psi}(\{0\})=0$; the spectrum is contained in $[0,\infty)$ because $H^{\mathrm{free}}=cA_{0}$ with $A_{0}\ge0$. Hence every vector is absolutely continuous, $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H^{\mathrm{free}})=H_{0}$, and there are no eigenvectors. This is (c) and completes the proof. [F1, F2, step 1.4, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is not claimed.** Ranges, asymptotic completeness and unitarity of
  $S$ are deliberately absent; they are the content of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] and
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]]. The Cook
  estimates are stated for Schwartz vectors exactly as in the cited
  mathematics; density then gives the strong limits on all of $H_{0}$.
- **Units.** The displayed Cook integrals carry the dimensions of the
  integrand times time; no numerical value of $m$, $\hbar$ or $V$ is asserted.

items.title: Asymptotic completeness and the unitary scattering operator for real bounded compactly supported potentials
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and a declared **compact-support-class**
potential $V$ supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Let $\Omega_{\pm}$ and $S$ be the
wave operators and scattering operator of clause (d) of that definition,
$E_{H}$ the projection valued measure of the self-adjoint interacting operator
$H$, and $\mu^{H}_{\psi}$ its scalar measures. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the wave operators exist by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]], and
$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{\pm}\subseteq H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and
$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$, where
$$H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H):=\{\psi\in H_{0}:\mu^{H}_{\psi}\ \text{is atomless and singular with respect to Lebesgue measure}\};$$

(b) each wave operator is asymptotically complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H);$$

(c) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the
free flow, $Se^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}S$ for
every $t\in\mathbb R$.

The statement is a conditional consequence of the declared model with a
compactly supported real bounded potential; it asserts no stationary amplitude,
no partial-wave decomposition, no cross section and no measured quantity.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared short-range scattering model with $m,\hbar>0$, spin zero and a compact-support-class potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$; the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Scaling correspondence.** With $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ and $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}$, the operators $A=-\Delta_{w}+M_{W}$ and $H$ on $W^{2,2}$ satisfy $H=cA$, $E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B)$ for every Borel $B$, the strong wave-operator limits in physical and nondimensional time coincide, and the sets $H_{\mathrm{ac}}$, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}$, $H_{\mathrm{pp}}$, $H_{\mathrm c}$ of $H$ and of $A$ are equal ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] clauses (a), (b), (d), (e)).

[F2] **Compact-support asymptotic completeness.** Assume Countable Choice. For real bounded $V_{0}$ with support in a ball, the nondimensional operator $-\Delta+M_{V_{0}}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ has wave operators with $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{\pm}\subseteq H_{\mathrm{ac}}$, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}=\{0\}$, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}=H_{\mathrm c}$, and $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ unitary and commuting with the free flow ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F3] **Scattering-state vocabulary.** The model reads its wave operators and $S$ exactly as the strong limits and the product of clause (d) of its definition, and reads asymptotic completeness as the equality of the ranges with $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)$ and $H_{\mathrm c}(H)$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (d)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; apply the nondimensional compact-support completeness theorem to the rescaled potential and transfer the range, spectral-subspace and unitarity statements to the model through the scaling correspondence.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 The declared potential $V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, so $W=V/c$ is real, bounded and supported in the same ball; hence [F2] applies to $W$. By [F1] the model's interacting operator is $H=cA$ with $A=-\Delta_{w}+M_{W}$ on the common domain. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 By [F2] the nondimensional wave operators exist with ranges inside $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A)$ and with $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A)=\{0\}$; by [F1] the physical strong limits exist exactly together with the nondimensional ones and coincide, and the spectral subspaces of $H$ and $A$ agree; this gives (a). [F1, F2, given]

2.1 By [F2], $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A)=H_{\mathrm c}(A)$ for the nondimensional operators; by [F1] the same displayed equalities hold with $H$ in place of $A$ and the same operators, which is (b). [F2, step 1.2, F1, algebra]

3.1 By [F2] the operator $\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ for the nondimensional pair is unitary and commutes with the free flow; since the physical and nondimensional wave operators coincide by [F1], $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary and commutes with $e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ for every $t$. This is (c) and completes the proof. [F2, step 2.1, F1, F3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **No uniform threshold statement.** The cited mathematics includes a threshold
  obstruction: for compactly supported potentials the compactness of the
  scattering defects fails uniformly at zero energy unless the energy cutoff
  vanishes there ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-scattering-defects]]).
  Completeness itself, as stated here, is not affected; the obstruction concerns
  the uniform compact-defect statement, not the range equalities.
- **Zero-energy scattering.** The theorem asserts nothing about the behaviour of
  the stationary solutions at $k=0$; every stationary statement of this page is
  made for $k>0$.

items.title: Asymptotic completeness for the resolvent-tail short-range class, with the decaying-tail example and the explicit exclusion of the Coulomb tail
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and a declared potential $V$ of the
**resolvent-tail class**: real $V=V_{2}+V_{\mathrm b}$ with
$V_{2}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ and $V_{\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{3})$
real, and, with the reduced potential $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}$ and the
nondimensional free operator $A_{0}:=-\Delta_{w}$ of the model,
$$h(r):=\bigl\|M_{W}(A_{0}-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\bigr\|,$$
finite for every $r\ge0$ and in $L^{1}([0,\infty))$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $H=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V}$ is self-adjoint on
$D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]); both wave operators
$$\Omega_{\pm}=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$$
exist as bounded linear isometries, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}
=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H)=H_{\mathrm c}(H)$, and $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(H)=\{0\}$;

(b) $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary on $H_{0}$;

(c) the conclusions of (a) and (b) hold in particular for a declared potential
of the explicit **decaying-tail form** $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$
with real $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ compactly supported and
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ almost everywhere for some
constants $C>0$, $\delta>0$; here the integrability hypothesis of the preamble
is not presupposed, because the cited theorem supplies it for this form;

(d) the explicit decaying-tail form of (c) does not cover the pure Coulomb
potential $V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$, $\kappa>0$: after any split into a compactly
supported $L^{2}$ part and a tail part, the bound
$|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ fails for every $\delta>0$,
because $\kappa(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}/|x|\to+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$. The pure Coulomb potential also fails the general resolvent-tail integrability hypothesis itself, as proved below; the Coulomb case is the separate
declared long-range model of this page.

The statement is conditional on the declared model with the displayed
integrability hypothesis and the cited mathematics; no cross section,
stationary amplitude or measured quantity is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared short-range scattering model with $m,\hbar>0$, spin zero and a resolvent-tail-class potential $V$; the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Scaling correspondence.** With $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ and $W=2mV/\hbar^{2}$, the operators $A_{0}=-\Delta_{w}$, $A=A_{0}+M_{W}$ and $H=cA$, $H^{\mathrm{free}}=cA_{0}$ on $W^{2,2}$ satisfy $E_{H}(cB)=E_{A}(B)$ for every Borel $B$, the physical and nondimensional wave-operator limits coincide, and the spectral subspaces $H_{\mathrm{ac}}$, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}$, $H_{\mathrm{pp}}$, $H_{\mathrm c}$ of $H$ and $A$ agree ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] clauses (a), (b), (d), (e)).

[F2] **Resolvent-tail short-range completeness.** Assume Countable Choice. For real $V_{0}=V_{0,2}+V_{0,\mathrm b}$ with $V_{0,2}\in L^{2}$, $V_{0,\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}$ real and $\|M_{V_{0}}(-\Delta-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}\|$ finite for every $r\ge0$ and integrable over $r\ge0$, the operator $-\Delta+M_{V_{0}}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ is self-adjoint, both ordinary wave operators exist, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}=\{0\}$, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}=H_{\mathrm c}$, and $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary; all conclusions hold for $V_{0}=V_{0,\mathrm{loc}}+V_{0,\mathrm{tail}}$ with compactly supported $L^{2}$ part and $|V_{0,\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$, $\delta>0$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-resolvent-tail-short-range-completeness]] clause display and its final paragraph).

[F3] **The model's readings.** The model's wave operators and scattering operator are the strong limits and the product of clause (d) of its definition, with the potential classes declared in clause (b) ([[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clauses (b), (d)).

[F4] A nonzero smooth bump supported in a fixed ball exists ([[lem-smooth-bump-between-concentric-euclidean-balls]]). Translation preserves complex $L^2$ norms ([[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]], first clause); on compact smooth functions the free operator is exactly $-\Delta$ on $H^2$ ([[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] (a) at $m=1/2$, $\hbar=1$). Coordinate differentiation commutes with translation by direct substitution in the derivative definition.

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the class hypothesis is exactly the nondimensional resolvent-tail hypothesis for the reduced potential, so the cited theorem applies, and the scaling correspondence transfers self-adjointness, the limits, the range equalities and the unitarity.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 Put $W:=2mV/\hbar^{2}=W_{2}+W_{\mathrm b}$ with $W_{2}:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V_{2}\in L^{2}$ and $W_{\mathrm b}:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V_{\mathrm b}\in L^{\infty}$, both real. The nondimensional free operator $A_{0}=-\Delta_{w}$ is the operator written $-\Delta$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ in [F2], and the class definition gives that $\|M_{W}(A_{0}-i)^{-1}\mathbf 1_{\{|\cdot|\ge r\}}\|$ is finite for every $r$ and integrable in $r$; hence [F2] applies with $V_{0}=W$ and gives: $A:=-\Delta+M_{W}$ is self-adjoint on $H^{2}$, both nondimensional wave operators exist, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}(A)=\{0\}$, $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{-}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(A)=H_{\mathrm c}(A)$, and $S_{\mathrm{nd}}=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is unitary. [F2, given, algebra]

1.2 [Failure of the general Coulomb resolvent-tail condition] For the pure Coulomb reduced potential put $W_C=-\gamma/|x|$, $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^2>0$. Fix by [F4] a nonzero real $\phi\in C_c^\infty(B_R)$, and for $r>R$ set $\phi_r(x)=\phi(x-2r e_1)$ and $f_r=(A_0-i)\phi_r$. Both are supported outside the radius-$r$ ball, since $2r-R>r$; derivatives do not enlarge support. The free derivative action and translation isometry give $\|\phi_r\|_2=\|\phi\|_2>0$ and $\|f_r\|_2=\|(A_0-i)\phi\|_2=:c_f>0$. Positivity and self-adjointness of $A_0$ ensure its resolvent at $i$ exists, and $(A_0-i)^{-1}\mathbf1_{\{|x|\ge r\}}f_r=\phi_r$. If the Coulomb resolvent-tail operator is not bounded at some radius it already fails the class; otherwise its operator norm obeys $h_C(r)\ge\frac{\|M_{W_C}\phi_r\|_2}{\|f_r\|_2}\ge\frac{\gamma\|\phi\|_2}{c_f(2r+R)}.$ The last bound uses $|x|\le2r+R$ on that support. The positive lower bound has divergent integral over $r>R$, so $h_C\notin L^1([0,\infty))$. Thus pure Coulomb fails the general class as well, proving the general-class exclusion in (d) without any zero-energy hypothesis. [F4, given, algebra]

2.1 By [F1] the model's operators are $H=cA$, $H^{\mathrm{free}}=cA_{0}$ on $W^{2,2}$ with $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, so $H$ is self-adjoint on $D(H)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the physical strong limits exist exactly when the nondimensional ones do and then coincide, and the subspaces $H_{\mathrm{ac}},H_{\mathrm{sc}},H_{\mathrm c}$ of $H$ and $A$ agree; moreover every operator $e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ is unitary, so for every $\psi$ the strong limit satisfies $\|\Omega_{\pm}\psi\|=\lim_{t\to\pm\infty}\|e^{itH/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\psi\|=\|\psi\|$, i.e. $\Omega_{\pm}$ are isometries. Combining with step 1.1 gives (a). [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F3] the model's operator $S$ is $\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ for the wave operators of step 2.1; by steps 1.1 and 2.1 these coincide with the nondimensional operators of [F2], whose product is unitary. Hence $S$ is unitary on $H_{0}$, which is (b). [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Let now $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$ with $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}$ compactly supported and $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}|\le C(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$, $\delta>0$; then $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V=W_{\mathrm{loc}}+W_{\mathrm{tail}}$ with $W_{\mathrm{loc}}:=(2m/\hbar^{2})V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}$ compactly supported and $|W_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le C'(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ with $C':=(2m/\hbar^{2})C$, so [F2]'s final paragraph gives all the conclusions of step 1.1 for this $W$ without the general integrability hypothesis; step 2.1 transfers them to $H$, so (a) and (b) hold for this $V$. This is (c). [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For $V(x)=-\kappa/|x|$ with $\kappa>0$ and any split $V=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$ into a compactly supported part and the remainder, the remainder equals $-\kappa/|x|$ for all sufficiently large $|x|$, so for every $\delta>0$ the quotient $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|=\kappa(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}/|x|$ tends to $+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$; hence no constant $C$ satisfies the sufficient decay bound of [F2]'s final paragraph, and the explicit form of (c) does not cover the Coulomb potential. This proves the sufficient-decay exclusion in (d). [F2, step 1.2, step 3.2, given, algebra] ∎


## Remarks

- **What the class excludes.** The resolvent-tail class excludes Coulomb's
  $\delta=0$ tail; the long-range comparison construction for the Coulomb
  potential is a separate declared model of this page
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-completeness]]).
- **Threshold.** No zero-energy nonresonance or absence-of-zero-eigenvalue
  hypothesis is imposed by the cited theorem; the item makes no statement about
  the stationary problem at $k=0$.

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Chapter 12 printed pages 257-284 (PDF pages 265-292): scattering by localized potentials and the S-matrix

items.title: The model's stationary scattering wave, its outgoing amplitude and the differential and total cross-section readings
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, with a **compact-support-class** potential
$V$ supported in the ball $B_{R}$, and adopt the declared stationary elastic
beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave number
$k>0$, direction $d\in S^2$ and the declared $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$ in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, with incident energy $E=\hbar^2k^2/(2m)$.
The construction below retains the dimensionless unit-incident shape
$\Psi$; its physical beam field is $\Phi=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$.
Put
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z):=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x):=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
for $f\in L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$ and $x\in B_{R}$. Assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $I+K_{k}$ is boundedly invertible on $L^{2}(B_{R};\mathbb C)$; with
$u:=(I+K_{k})^{-1}\bigl(e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}\bigr)$ and
$$\Psi(x):=e^{ikd\cdot x}-\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)u(y)\,dy,$$
one has $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^{3})$,
$(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ distributionally on $\mathbb R^{3}$, and
$\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$;

(b) with $r=|x|>2R$ and $\Omega=x/r$, the **scattering amplitude**
$$f_{k}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)\,dy$$
is smooth on $S^{2}$ and
$$\Psi(x)=e^{ikd\cdot x}+\frac{e^{ikr}f_{k}(\Omega)}{r}+\mathcal E(x),$$
where $|\mathcal E(x)|+|\partial_{r}\mathcal E(x)|\le C(k,R,\|Wu\|_{1})r^{-2}$
uniformly in $\Omega$, and for every fixed product $D_{\Omega}$ of smooth
tangential differential operators on $S^{2}$ also
$|D_{\Omega}\mathcal E|+|D_{\Omega}\partial_{r}\mathcal E|\le C_{D}r^{-2}$;

(c) the physical scattered radial current of the beam model, with
$\Phi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}(\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x})$, is
$$j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}(r,\Omega)=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\left(\frac{\hbar k}{m}\frac{|f_k(\Omega)|^2}{r^2}+O(r^{-3})\right)$$
uniformly in $\Omega$, with physical incident flux density
$J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$;
the common density factor cancels, and the cross-section readings are
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\Omega)=|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}, \qquad \sigma=\int_{S^{2}}|f_{k}(\Omega)|^{2}\,d\Omega<\infty\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}};$$

(d) the solution $\Psi$ of (a) is a generalized stationary solution of the
beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$ in the sense of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]], and no other
function satisfying the same equation on the complement of
$\operatorname{supp}V$ and the same outgoing reading is produced by the
construction.

Every assertion is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. The stationary wave is not an element of the state space; the
item asserts no preparation, no beam apparatus, no detector acceptance and no
measured count rate.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared model and beam model with $m,\hbar>0$, compact-support-class $V$ supported in $B_{R}$, wave number $k>0$, direction $d$, density scale $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$, reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, kernel $G_{k}$, operator $K_{k}$ and choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Stationary outgoing integral and flux.** Assume Countable Choice. Let $R>0$, real $V_{0}\in L^{\infty}$ with support in $B_{R}$ and $k>0$; with $K_{k}$ built from $V_{0}$ and $G_{k}$ as above (with $V_{0}$ in place of $W$), the operator $I+K_{k}$ is boundedly invertible, $u=(I+K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, $\Psi=e_{\mathrm{inc}}-\int G_{k}(\cdot-y)V_{0}(y)u(y)dy$ satisfies $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, $(-\Delta+V_{0}-k^{2})\Psi=0$ distributionally and $\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$; the amplitude $f_{k}(\Omega)=-(4\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}V_{0}(y)u(y)dy$ is smooth with the displayed uniform far-field and derivative bounds, and the scattered radial current and cross-section displays hold ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-outgoing-integral-and-flux]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **Fredholm invertibility.** Assume Countable Choice. For real bounded compactly supported $V_{0}$ and every $k>0$, the operator $I+K_{k}$ of [F1] is boundedly invertible ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-outgoing-fredholm-invertibility]]).

[F3] **Scaling correspondence.** With $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, the model's energy operator satisfies $H=cA$, $A=-\Delta_{w}+M_{W}$ with $W=2mV/\hbar^{2}$; the physical energy $E$ and the nondimensional spectral value $k^{2}$ correspond by $E=ck^{2}$, i.e. $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F4] **Unit-shape and physical current readings.** The mathematical current functional is $\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]=(\hbar/m)\operatorname{Im}(\overline\psi\nabla\psi)$. For the unit incident shape its value is $(\hbar k/m)d$, and for the exact outgoing shape $fe^{ikr}/r$ its radial value is $(\hbar k/m)|f|^2/r^2$ ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-three-dimensional-current-and-flux]] clause (c)). For the declared constant $n_{\mathrm{inc}}>0$, the beam model reads the physical field as $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi$, so the quadratic functional gives $\mathbf j[\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\psi]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\mathbf j^{\mathrm{unit}}[\psi]$, and its cross sections are ratios with $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] (b)-(d)).

[F5] **The beam model's solubility vocabulary.** A generalized stationary solution is a $C^{2}$ function on the complement of $\operatorname{supp}V$ satisfying the stationary equation there with an outgoing asymptotic reading and a scattering amplitude read in metres ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] clause (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the physical stationary equation divided by $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ is the nondimensional equation with potential $W$, so the cited mathematical stationary theorem applies verbatim and its amplitude and flux displays are exactly the model's readings.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 Since $V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, so is $W=2mV/\hbar^{2}$, which is read in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$; dividing the physical stationary equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta\Psi+V\Psi=E\Psi$ by $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ gives $-\Delta\Psi+W\Psi=(E/c)\Psi$, and $E/c=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)\cdot2m/\hbar^{2}=k^{2}$ by [F3] with $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The kernel $G_{k}(x-y)W(y)$ on $B_{R}\times B_{R}$ is square-integrable because $|x-y|^{-2}$ is locally integrable in three dimensions and $B_{R}$ is bounded, so $K_{k}$ is Hilbert-Schmidt and [F2] gives bounded invertibility of $I+K_{k}$; [F1] then gives $\Psi\in H^{2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$, the distributional equation $(-\Delta+W-k^{2})\Psi=0$ and $\Psi|_{B_{R}}=u$, which is (a). [F2, F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F1] the smooth amplitude $f_{k}(\Omega)=-(4\pi)^{-1}\int e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u(y)dy$ and the uniform expansion with the $r^{-2}$ remainder and its tangential and radial derivative bounds hold; these are exactly the displays of (b), with the constant depending on $k,R$ and $\|Wu\|_{1}$. [F1, step 2.1]

4.1 By [F1] the unit-shape scattered field $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=\Psi-e^{ikd\cdot x}$ has radial mathematical current $(\hbar k/m)|f_k|^2/r^2+O(r^{-3})$ uniformly. Write $\Psi_{\mathrm{sc}}=u+iv$; the physical field has real and imaginary parts $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u,\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v$. Since the scale is constant, its current is $(\hbar/m)[(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)\nabla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)-(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}v)\nabla(\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}u)]=n_{\mathrm{inc}}(\hbar/m)(u\nabla v-v\nabla u)$ by [F4]. Thus the physical scattered current is the display in (c), and the same calculation on the unit incident plane wave gives $J_{\mathrm{inc}}=n_{\mathrm{inc}}\hbar k/m>0$. Dividing yields $\lim_{r\to\infty}r^2j_r^{\mathrm{sc}}/J_{\mathrm{inc}}=|f_k|^2$. Smoothness and boundedness of $f_k$ on the sphere, with [F1]'s uniform error, give the finite total cross section $\sigma=\int_{S^2}|f_k|^2d\Omega$. The unit-shape amplitude stays in metres and the density cancels from both cross-section readings. This is (c). [F1, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By step 2.1 and step 3.1 the constructed $\Psi$ is $C^{2}$ on the complement of the essential closed support of $V$: near each such point the convolution integrates the compactly supported $L^1$ density $Wu$ against $G_k(x-y)$ at a positive distance from its singularity, so its derivatives of every fixed order are bounded on a smaller neighborhood and differentiation under that integral is valid; the incident exponential is smooth too, satisfies the stationary equation there and has the outgoing reading with amplitude $f_{k}$ in metres; by [F5] it is a generalized stationary solution of the beam model at energy $E$ and direction $d$, and the construction determines it through the explicit invertible problem, so no other function with the same equation and outgoing reading arises from this construction. This is (d) and completes the proof. [F5, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is read, and what is not.** The amplitude and cross sections are
  computed from the explicitly constructed stationary field; the pair asserts
  nothing about a preparation that would realize the incident plane-wave
  reading, and no measured count rate is predicted. Converting these model
  quantities into an expected count rate requires a declared target, fluence
  and detector model with its own uncertainties.
- **Normalization.** With physical coordinates $x$ in metres and $k$ in
  inverse metres, the unit-incident shape $\Psi$ is dimensionless, the reduced
  potential $W=(2m/\hbar^2)V$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$, and the displayed
  integral for $f_k$ has dimension length. The physical beam field
  $\sqrt{n_{\mathrm{inc}}}\Psi$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-3/2}}$; its number currents
  are in $\mathrm{m^{-2}s^{-1}}$. The common density factor cancels, leaving
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,sr^{-1}}$ independently of its value.

items.title: The model's partial-wave and phase-shift vocabulary for a declared central potential
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and its stationary elastic beam model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]] at wave
number $k>0$; adopt the declared central-potential reading of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-central-potential-model]]: a **declared central
potential** of the pair is a real bounded measurable $V(x)=v(|x|)$ with
$v:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ bounded, and it is **short-range** when it lies in
the compact-support class of the scattering model. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]; the wave number $k$ is read in
$\mathrm{m^{-1}}$ and the energy $E=\hbar^{2}k^{2}/(2m)$ in joules.

**(b) Channel vocabulary.** For a declared central short-range potential $V$
and a channel label $(l,m)$ with $l\ge0$ and $-l\le m\le l$, the model
declares the **partial wave** $l$ and reads the angular dependence in the
complete spherical harmonic family $(Y_{lm})$ of
[[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]]; the
labels $l,m$ are indices of that family. The reduced equation below is read in
the pair's nondimensional normalization: the reduced potential is
$w:=2mv/\hbar^{2}$ of clause (c) of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] and the energy is $k^{2}$,
so that the physical parameters $m,\hbar$ do not enter it explicitly. The
model declares the **regular radial solution**
$\varphi_{l}$ of the reduced equation
$$-\varphi_{l}''+\Bigl(w(r)+\frac{l(l+1)}{r^{2}}\Bigr)\varphi_{l}=k^{2}\varphi_{l}, \qquad \varphi_{l}(r)/r^{l+1}\longrightarrow1\quad(r\to0),$$
and the **outgoing radial solution** $f_{l}$ with
$$f_{l}(r)=e^{i(kr-l\pi/2)}\bigl(1+O(r^{-1})\bigr)\qquad(r\to\infty)$$
outside the interaction region; these are the functions constructed by the
cited theorem, and they are not asserted to be elements of the state space.

**(c) Channel factor and phase shift.** The model declares the **channel
factor** and the **phase shift** of the partial wave $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(k):=\frac{\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}}{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}, \qquad S_{l}(k)=e^{2i\delta_{l}(k)},$$
where $W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})=\varphi_{l}f_{l}'-\varphi_{l}'f_{l}$ is the
Wronskian and $\delta_{l}(k)$ is the **phase shift**, a real number read
modulo $\pi$; the model reads $|S_{l}(k)|=1$ and calls the channel
**elastic**. The declared **channel cross-section reading** is
$$\sigma_{l}(k):=\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k),$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The existence of the functions and the identities
$|S_{l}|=1$ and $\sum_{l}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}<\infty$ are proved on this
page and are not presupposed here.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: names
for the objects constructed by the cited mathematics and the reading of the
phase shift modulo $\pi$. The model asserts no identification of the labels
$l,m$ with a measured angular momentum of a material system, no statement
about bound states or their count, and no channel decomposition for
non-central potentials. Every numerical statement about $\delta_{l}$ is a
separate theorem or example of the pair.

## Remarks

- **Modulo $\pi$.** The phase shift is read modulo $\pi$, since
  $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ determines $\delta_{l}$ only up to an integer
  multiple of $\pi$; every display of this page that uses $\delta_{l}$ is
  insensitive to that ambiguity, as $\sin^{2}$ is.
- **Non-central potentials.** For a non-central declared potential the pair
  asserts no diagonal channel factor; the on-shell operator of the following
  theorem is then a general unitary on $L^{2}(S^{2})$.
