items.title: The declared single-channel resonance model: pole-shaped channel factor and its cross-section reading
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and action constant $\hbar>0$, and its partial-wave and phase-shift
reading [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] for a
declared central short-range potential. Fix a **channel label** $l\in\{0,1,2,\dots\}$
in the sense of clause (b) of that reading. Units are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]].

**(b) The declared single-channel resonance model.** As an additional model
assumption of the pair, fix real **resonance parameters** $E_{r}$ and
$\Gamma>0$, both read in joules, and **declare** the channel factor of the
label $l$ to be
$$S_{l}(E):=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}\qquad(E>0),$$
read for positive energies only, with the **phase shift** of the channel read
from the relation $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ modulo $\pi$ and the **channel
cross-section reading**
$$\sigma_{l}(E):=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E), \qquad k(E):=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^{2}}$. The model calls $E_{r}$ the **resonance energy** and
$\Gamma$ the **width parameter**; both are declared model parameters and
neither is identified with a measured quantity. The parameter $E_r$ may be
zero or negative; calling it a resonance energy does not assign a physical
cross section at that parameter value unless $E_r>0$. Auxiliary real-axis
algebraic comparisons of the Lorentzian factor do not extend $k(E)$ or
$\sigma_l(E)$ beyond the positive-energy domain.

**(c) Status and scope.** Clauses (a)-(b) declare a conditional one-channel
model. The pair asserts no analytic continuation, no pole of the resolvent and
no property of any potential that would produce the declared factor
$S_{l}$; the model is used only to compute the induced phase shift and channel
cross section of the declared factor. In particular, no exponential decay law,
no lifetime $\hbar/\Gamma$ and no Lorentzian line shape of a measured
distribution is asserted or derived; those would be separate models with their
own assumptions and their own uncertainty qualifications.

## Remarks

- **Relation to the full cross section.** Substituting the declared channel
  factor into the phase-shift series of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] produces a conditional
  total cross section for an idealized situation in which a single channel
  dominates; the pair does not assert that any declared potential has that
  behavior.
- **Width versus rate.** The width parameter $\Gamma$ is an energy parameter
  of the declared factor, not a decay rate; the identification of $\Gamma$
  with a rate times $\hbar$ requires a separate decay model and is not made
  here.

items.title: Partial-wave expansion, unit-modulus channel factors and the phase-shift cross-section series
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **declared central short-range potential** $V(x)=v(|x|)$ in the
sense of [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]]
clause (a): $v$ is real, bounded and $V$ is supported in a ball $B_{R}$. Adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, with amplitude $f_{k}$ as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], and the
channel vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b),
(c). Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) $f_{k}$ depends only on $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and its **Legendre
expansion**
$$f_{k}(\theta)=\frac{1}{2ik}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\bigl(S_{l}(k)-1\bigr)P_{l}(\cos\theta)$$
converges in $L^{2}(S^{2})$ and absolutely, so the model's cross-section
reading is
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}(\theta)=|f_{k}(\theta)|^{2};$$

(b) the channel factors are unit modulus, $|S_{l}(k)|=1$, the phase shifts
$\delta_{l}(k)$ are real modulo $\pi$, and the **total cross section** of the
beam model is
$$\sigma=\frac{\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)|S_{l}(k)-1|^{2} =\frac{4\pi}{k^{2}}\sum_{l\ge0}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(k)\qquad\text{in }\mathrm{m^{2}},$$
the series converging, with the channel readings of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c) as
its summands;

(c) the objects $\varphi_{l}$, $f_{l}$, $S_{l}$ and $\delta_{l}$ of the
channel vocabulary are exactly the regular and outgoing radial solutions, the
Wronskian ratio and the phase shift constructed by the cited mathematics for
the reduced radial potential $w=(2m/\hbar^2)v$ at the model's wave number $k$; the phase shifts
are not asserted to have a definite sign and no low-energy limit is asserted
beyond the convergence of the series.

The statement is conditional on the declared central model, the beam model
and the cited mathematics; it asserts no measured angular distribution and no
identification of $l$ with a measured angular momentum.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared central short-range potential $V=v(|\cdot|)$ supported in $B_{R}$, the wave number $k>0$, the direction $d$, the amplitude $f_{k}$ of the stationary theorem, and the channel vocabulary of the pair.

[F1] **Partial-wave cross-section convergence.** Assume Countable Choice. For real bounded central $V_{0}$ supported in $B_{R}$ and $k>0$, with $f$ the amplitude of the stationary outgoing solution, $f$ depends only on $\cos\theta$, its Legendre expansion with $S_{l}$ equals $\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ converges in $L^{2}(S^{2})$ and absolutely, $|S_{l}|=1$, and the total cross section equals the phase-shift series ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **The model's amplitude and cross-section reading.** The stationary theorem of the pair constructs the model's amplitude $f_{k}$ and reads $d\sigma/d\Omega=|f_{k}|^{2}$ and $\sigma=\int|f_{k}|^{2}$, and the channel vocabulary declares $\varphi_{l},f_{l},S_{l},\delta_{l}$ and $\sigma_{l}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] clauses (b), (c), [[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b), (c)).

[F3] **The equation in nondimensional form.** Dividing the physical stationary equation by $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$ gives the nondimensional equation with the reduced central potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V=v_{W}(|\cdot|)$, and the physical wave number $k$ equals the nondimensional one ([[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] clauses (a), (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; reduce the physical stationary problem to its nondimensional form, note that centrality is preserved, and instantiate the cited partial-wave theorem, whose amplitude is the model's amplitude.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 By [F3] the physical stationary problem at wave number $k$ and reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ is the nondimensional problem with $W(x)=w(|x|)$, $w=(2m/\hbar^{2})v$, which is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$; hence $W$ is a central potential of the class of [F1]. [F3, given, algebra]

2.1 By [F2] the model's amplitude $f_{k}$ is the amplitude of the stationary outgoing solution of the nondimensional problem of step 1.1, so [F1] gives that $f_{k}$ depends only on $\cos\theta$, that its Legendre expansion has the displayed coefficients $S_{l}$ and converges in $L^{2}(S^{2})$ and absolutely, and by [F2] the model reads $d\sigma/d\Omega=|f_{k}|^{2}$. This is (a). [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1] the factors satisfy $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ with $|S_{l}|=1$ for real $\delta_{l}$ modulo $\pi$, and the total cross section equals the displayed phase-shift series; substituting the model's channel readings $\sigma_{l}=(4\pi/k^{2})(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}$ from [F2] exhibits the series as the sum of the channel readings, and its convergence is [F1]'s. This is (b). [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Since the nondimensional problem of step 1.1 has the same reduced radial equation and the same wave number $k$ as the model's channel vocabulary, the functions $\varphi_{l},f_{l}$ and the Wronskian ratio $S_{l}=\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$ of the vocabulary are exactly those constructed by [F1]; the phase shift is the half-argument $\delta_{l}$ modulo $\pi$ by definition of the vocabulary, and no sign or low-energy statement is added. This is (c) and completes the proof. [F1, step 1.1, F2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Resonance models.** A single-channel model of the phase shift is declared
  and analysed separately on this page
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]]); this theorem
  asserts nothing about the existence of resonances for a given potential.
- **Low-energy behaviour.** The series converges for every $k>0$ of the
  declared class; no statement is made about its behaviour as $k\to0$, where
  the class hypotheses themselves remain in force but the pair asserts no
  limiting formula.

items.title: The controlled Born reading: operator-norm condition, uniform amplitude error and coupling scaling
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$, adopt
the stationary elastic beam model at wave number $k>0$ and direction
$d\in S^{2}$, and let
$$W:=\frac{2m}{\hbar^{2}}V,\qquad G_{k}(z)=\frac{e^{ik|z|}}{4\pi|z|},\qquad (K_{k}f)(x)=\int_{B_{R}}G_{k}(x-y)W(y)f(y)\,dy$$
and $u=(I+K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, $f_{k}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]], with
$e_{\mathrm{inc}}=e^{ikd\cdot x}|_{B_{R}}$. Put $q:=\|K_{k}\|$, the operator
norm of [[def-operator-norm]] and [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], and
$$f_{B}(\Omega):=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{ik(d-\Omega)\cdot y}W(y)\,dy$$
for $\Omega\in S^{2}$, read in metres. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]).
Then:

(a) the operator $K_{k}$ is bounded, $q<\infty$, and if $q<1$ the exact
stationary solution satisfies
$$\bigl\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})};$$

(b) under the same condition $q<1$ the **Born amplitude** $f_{B}$ approximates
the exact amplitude uniformly,
$$\bigl|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)\bigr|\le \frac{\|W\|_{\infty}\,|B_{R}|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\,\frac{q}{1-q}\, \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})} \qquad(\Omega\in S^{2}),$$
with $|B_{R}|=4\pi R^{3}/3$;

(c) *coupling scaling.* For a real or complex multiplier $\eta$ with
$|\eta|q<1$, let $u_{\eta}:=(I+\eta K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$, let
$f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d):=-\eta(4\pi)^{-1}\int_{B_R}e^{-ik\Omega\cdot y}W(y)u_\eta(y;d)\,dy$ be the amplitude for the scaled potential $\eta W$, and let $f_{B}$ be as above. Then
$$\bigl\|u_{\eta}-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{2}\le\frac{|\eta|q}{1-|\eta|q} \bigl\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\bigr\|_{2},\qquad \sup_{\Omega,d\in S^{2}}\bigl|f_{k,\eta}(\Omega;d)-\eta f_{B}(\Omega;d)\bigr| \le\frac{|\eta|^{2}\|W\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|q}{4\pi(1-|\eta|q)};$$
in particular no condition on the base operator norm of $K_{k}$ itself is
needed for (c).

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited mathematics;
the condition $q<1$ is an operator-norm condition on the declared potential,
kernel and wave number, not a vague smallness of $V$, and no measured cross
section is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared model and beam model with $m,\hbar>0$, compact-support-class $V$ supported in $B_{R}$, wave number $k>0$, direction $d$, the reduced potential $W$, kernel $G_{k}$, operator $K_{k}$, exact solution $u$ and amplitude $f_{k}$ of the stationary theorem, Born amplitude $f_{B}$, $q=\|K_{k}\|$, and the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Controlled Born amplitude error.** Assume Countable Choice. Adopt the hypotheses and notation of the nondimensional stationary outgoing integral theorem for a real bounded potential $V_{0}$ supported in $B_{R}$: $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $u=(I+K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$ and $f_{k}$ the amplitude. If $q<1$, then $\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}$ and $|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)|\le\frac{\|V_{0}\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\frac{q}{1-q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}$ uniformly in $\Omega$; for $V_{\eta}=\eta V_{0}$ with $|\eta|q<1$ the scaling displays hold with $u_{\eta}=(I+\eta K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$ and the same amplitude integrals, for real and complex $\eta$, with no base condition on $q$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-controlled-born-amplitude-error]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **The model's stationary solution.** The model's $u$, $\Psi$ and amplitude $f_{k}$ are those of the stationary theorem of the pair, constructed from the reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ and the same kernel and operator $K_{k}$ ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] clauses (a), (b), [[lem-nrqm-scattering-model-scaling-correspondence]] clauses (a), (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the nondimensional controlled Born theorem with the model's reduced potential, then rewrite its constants in the model's symbols.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F2].

1.1 The reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, and by [F2] the model's $K_{k}$, $u$ and $f_{k}$ are exactly the objects of [F1] for $V_{0}=W$; hence [F1] applies with $q=\|K_{k}\|<\infty$. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 If $q<1$, [F1] gives $\|u-e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}\le\frac{q}{1-q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}$, which is (a). [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Under the same condition, [F1]'s uniform estimate with $V_{0}=W$ is $|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)|\le\frac{\|W\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|^{1/2}}{4\pi}\frac{q}{1-q}\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{2}$ for every $\Omega\in S^{2}$, which is the display of (b) since $|B_{R}|=4\pi R^{3}/3$ for the ball. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For real or complex $\eta$ with $|\eta|q<1$, [F1]'s scaling clause gives the two displays of (c) with $u_{\eta}=(I+\eta K_{k})^{-1}e_{\mathrm{inc}}$ and the same amplitude integrals; the constants are exactly $\|W\|_{\infty}$, $|B_{R}|$ and $q$, and no base smallness condition beyond $|\eta|q<1$ is used. This completes the proof. [F1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading the condition.** In the model's variables the condition of (a)-(b)
  is the operator-norm condition $q=\|K_{k}\|<1$ on the declared potential,
  radius and wave number; the examples of this pair verify it for a uniform
  ball potential through an explicit Hilbert-Schmidt bound of the kernel, so
  no vague smallness of the potential is used.
- **Complex coupling.** The scaling form is algebraic in $\eta$ and does not
  use the real-potential flux conclusions; for complex $\eta$ the pair
  asserts no unitarity or cross-section reading of the resulting amplitude
  beyond the displayed estimate.

items.title: Identification of the model's scattering operator with the on-shell stationary operator, and the central per-channel form
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero and a **compact-support-class** potential $V$ supported in $B_{R}$; by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] the model's
wave operators exist and
$$S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$$
is unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow. Write $\sigma$ for
surface measure on $S^{2}$ and $\mathfrak h=L^{2}(S^{2},d\sigma)$, and for
every $d\in S^{2}$ let $f_{k}(\cdot,d)$ be the model's stationary amplitude
of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] at incident
direction $d$, with the operator $\mathcal A_{k}$ on $\mathfrak h$ defined by
$$(\mathcal A_{k}a)(\Omega):=\int_{S^{2}}f_{k}(\Omega,d)\,a(d)\,d\sigma(d).$$
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the free flow is diagonalized by the free trace transform of the cited
mathematics, a unitary $F_{0}:H_{0}\to L^{2}((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$ with
$(F_{0}g)(E,\omega)=E^{1/4}2^{-1/2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\,\omega)$ in the
nondimensional variables of the scaling correspondence, and the model's
scattering operator is carried into multiplication,
$$F_{0}\,S\,F_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)};$$

(b) for almost every $E=k^{2}>0$ the on-shell operator is
$$S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k},$$
a unitary operator on $\mathfrak h$, and the model's stationary amplitude
$f_{k}(\Omega,d)$ is the kernel of $\mathcal A_{k}$;

(c) for $R\in SO(3)$ let $V_{R}(x):=V(R^{-1}x)$ and $(U_{R}a)(\omega):=a(R^{-1}\omega)$;
then
$$S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}\,S[V](E)\,U_{R}^{-1};$$

(d) if $V$ is in addition central, the fiber decomposes in the spherical
harmonic basis as $S(E)Y_{lm}=S_{l}(k)Y_{lm}$, where $S_{l}$ and
$\delta_{l}$ are the model's channel factor and phase shift of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]], equal to the
Wronskian ratio $\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$, and
the cross-section reading of
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] is the phase-shift series
of that channel decomposition.

The statement identifies operators and operators-valued functions of the
declared model; it asserts no measurement of $S$ or $S(E)$, no detector model
and no empirical claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared model with $m,\hbar>0$, compact-support-class $V$ supported in $B_{R}$; the model's wave operators, scattering operator and stationary amplitude; the free trace transform $F_{0}$; the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Stationary and dynamical sector identification.** Assume Countable Choice. For real bounded compactly supported $V_{0}$, with $H_{0}=-\Delta$, $H=H_{0}+M_{V_{0}}$ and $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ its complete scattering operator, the free trace transform $F_{0}g(E,\omega)=E^{1/4}2^{-1/2}\widehat g(\sqrt E\omega)$ is unitary onto $L^{2}((0,\infty),dE;\mathfrak h)$, $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ with $S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k}$ unitary, $\mathcal A_{k}$ built from the stationary amplitude, $S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}S[V](E)U_{R}^{-1}$, and for radial $V_{0}$ the fiber is diagonal with $S_{l}(E)=\overline{W_{l}}/W_{l}$, $|S_{l}|=1$ ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-stationary-dynamical-sector-identification]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d)).

[F2] **The model's amplitude and $S$.** The model's amplitude $f_{k}(\cdot,d)$ is the stationary theorem's amplitude for the reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, and the model's $S=\Omega_{+}^{*}\Omega_{-}$ is the unitary operator of the compact-support completeness theorem ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]] clause (b), [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c)).

[F3] **The channel vocabulary.** For a central short-range potential the model declares $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}=\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$ and $\sigma_{l}=(4\pi/k^{2})(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; the model's operators and amplitude are the cited nondimensional ones through the scaling correspondence, so the nondimensional identification theorem applies and supplies all four clauses.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 The reduced potential $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$ is real, bounded and supported in $B_{R}$, so [F1] applies to it; by the scaling correspondence the model's operators $H^{\mathrm{free}},H$ are $cA_{0},cA$ with $A_{0}=-\Delta$, $A=-\Delta+M_{W}$ and the physical and nondimensional wave operators coincide. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 By [F2] the model's stationary amplitude for direction $d$ is the amplitude of [F1]'s stationary problem for $W$ at the same wave number $k$; hence $\mathcal A_{k}$ is exactly the on-shell amplitude operator of [F1]. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 By [F1] the free trace transform $F_{0}$ diagonalizes the free flow and $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ with $S(E)=I+\frac{ik}{2\pi}\mathcal A_{k}$; since the model's $S$ and $\mathcal A_{k}$ are the same operators as in [F1] by steps 1.1 and 2.1, the displays of (a) and (b) follow, including unitarity of the on-shell operator. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F1] the covariance identity $S[V_{R}](E)=U_{R}S[V](E)U_{R}^{-1}$ holds for the nondimensional potential; since rotations act on $W$ exactly as on $V$ through $R^{-1}$, the same identity is the model's (c). [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 If $V$ is central, so is $W$; [F1] gives $S(E)Y_{lm}=S_{l}(k)Y_{lm}$ with $S_{l}=\overline{W_{l}}/W_{l}$; by [F3] the model's channel vocabulary names exactly these objects $S_{l}=\overline{W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})}/W(\varphi_{l},f_{l})$ and $\delta_{l}$, and the phase-shift series of the partial-wave theorem is the total cross-section reading of this decomposition. This is (d) and completes the proof. [F1, F3, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the identification is.** The identity $F_{0}SF_{0}^{*}=M_{S(E)}$ is an
  operator identity for the declared model; it is the precise sense in which
  the pair may speak of "the S-matrix at energy $E$", and it makes no claim
  that any apparatus measures $S(E)$.
- **Non-central potentials.** For a non-central potential no individual
  spherical-harmonic channel is asserted; only the covariance of (c) holds.

items.title: The declared long-range Coulomb model and its Dollard-modified free comparison
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Framework data.** Adopt the state and composition postulate P1, the
observable and probability postulate P2, the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4,
the kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5 and the
identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), with the spin-zero
state space $H_{0}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, mass $m>0$, action
constant $\hbar>0$ and the units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

**(b) The declared Coulomb model.** As an additional model assumption of the
pair, fix a **coupling** $\kappa>0$, read in $\mathrm{J\,m}$, and adopt the
**one-centre Coulomb model** of
[[def-nrqm-central-framework-coulomb-and-hydrogen-model]] in its spin-zero
one-particle reading: the declared potential is
$$V_{\kappa}(x):=-\frac{\kappa}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),$$
read in joules, with the value at the origin a declared convention that does
not affect the theory, and the **assigned energy observable** is
$$H_{\kappa}=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}-\frac{\kappa}{|\cdot|}$$
on the domain $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$,
self-adjoint there by
[[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] clause (a) with flow
$e^{-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]. The model declares the
free comparison operator to be the free assigned energy observable
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$ of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (c), and reads its
Coulomb coupling in the inverse-length form
$$\gamma:=\frac{2m\kappa}{\hbar^{2}}\quad(\mathrm{m^{-1}}), \qquad\text{so that}\qquad H_{\kappa}=c\Bigl(-\Delta_{w}-\frac{\gamma}{|\cdot|}\Bigr),\quad c=\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}.$$
The pure Coulomb potential is **not** in the short-range classes of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b); it is the
model's long-range case.

**(c) The declared Dollard-modified comparison.** Choose a reference length $\ell_\star>0$, read in metres, as a comparison convention, and put
$$t_{\star}:=\frac{2m\ell_\star^2}{\hbar}\quad(\mathrm{s}).$$
and, for $t\ne0$, let $h_{t}:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be the bounded Borel
function
$$h_{t}(x):=\exp\Bigl(i\,\operatorname{sign}(t)\, \frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mx}}\,\log\frac{|t|}{t_{\star}}\Bigr)\quad(x>0), \qquad h_{t}(0):=1 .$$
The model declares the **Dollard-modified free comparison** to be the family
$$U_{D}(t):=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}\,h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})\quad(t\ne0), \qquad U_{D}(0):=I,$$
where $h_{t}(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ is the bounded functional calculus
([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]] clause 1) of the self-adjoint free
operator: since $h_{t}$ is unimodular, $U_{D}(t)$ is unitary for every $t$,
and both factors are functions of $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and commute. The
**modified wave operators** of the model are the strong limits
$$\Omega_{D\pm}:=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}U_{D}(t),$$
declared when both exist, and the **modified scattering operator** is
$S_{D}:=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ when both exist and are isometries. The
reference length and the resulting time $t_\star$ are declared conventions. More exactly, changing the reference time from $t_\star$ to $t_\star'$ multiplies $U_D(t)$ on the right, for each sign $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, by the fixed free-energy unitary
$$Q_\sigma= q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}}),\qquad q_\sigma(E)=\exp\Bigl(-i\sigma\frac{m\kappa}{\hbar\sqrt{2mE}}\log\frac{t_\star'}{t_\star}\Bigr)\quad(E>0),\qquad q_\sigma(0)=1.$$
It is a bounded unimodular Borel multiplier and commutes with the free flow. Hence, when the wave operators exist, $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. The completeness and isometry properties are unchanged; these are the fixed outgoing and incoming phase conventions.

**(d) Status and scope.** Clauses (b)-(c) are declarations of the pair: a
prescribed long-range potential with its assigned energy observable, and a
modified comparison construction for it. The model asserts no formula for a
Coulomb scattering amplitude, no Rutherford cross section and no measured
quantity; the modification is a comparison construction for the long-range
generator, not a new interaction or a measured force. The ordinary
short-range comparison of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (d) is not claimed
to be complete for the Coulomb model; its completeness is established only
for the modified comparison, on this page.

## Remarks

- **Why a modified comparison is needed.** The free comparison
  $e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ does not have a
  complete strong limit in general for a $1/|x|$ tail: the classical phase
  mismatch of the long-range interaction is not integrable in time. The
  logarithmic phase of $h_{t}$ is the declared correction; the model does not
  derive it from a measured force law.
- **Units of the phase.** The exponent is dimensionless: $m\kappa/(\hbar\sqrt{2mx})$
  is dimensionless for $x$ in joules, and $\log(|t|/t_{\star})$ is
  dimensionless for $t$ in seconds and $t_{\star}=2m\ell_\star^2/\hbar$ in seconds. Indeed $m/\hbar$ has dimension $\mathrm{s\,m^{-2}}$, and the reference length squared supplies the missing $\mathrm{m^2}$. The quantity $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^2$ has inverse-length units; its numerical coefficient becomes dimensionless only after a length unit is fixed.

items.title: Completeness of the Dollard-modified wave operators for the declared Coulomb model
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared long-range Coulomb model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin zero,
action constant $\hbar>0$, coupling $\kappa>0$, the assigned energy operator
$H_{\kappa}$ on $H^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$, the free operator
$H^{\mathrm{free}}$, the inverse-length coupling
$\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$, a declared reference length $\ell_\star>0$ in metres and reference time $t_{\star}=2m\ell_\star^2/\hbar$, the
Dollard-modified comparison $U_{D}(t)$ and the modified wave operators
$\Omega_{D\pm}$ and $S_{D}$ of that definition. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Then:

(a) the modified wave operators exist as strong limits and are bounded linear
isometries, $\Omega_{D\pm}^{*}\Omega_{D\pm}=I$, and they intertwine,
$$\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}=e^{-isH_{\kappa}/\hbar}\Omega_{D\pm} \qquad(s\in\mathbb R);$$

(b) the modified wave operators are complete,
$$\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D+}=\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D-} =H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\kappa})=H_{\mathrm c}(H_{\kappa});$$

(c) the modified scattering operator $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is
unitary on $H_{0}$ and commutes with the free flow;

(d) the ordinary short-range comparison of the model is not substituted:
neither existence nor completeness of
$\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to\pm\infty}e^{itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$
is asserted, and the modification is essential to the statement.

The statement is conditional on the declared model and the cited
mathematics. It asserts no explicit Coulomb scattering amplitude, no
Rutherford or other cross section, and no measured quantity; the logarithmic
phase is a comparison construction for the long-range generator.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared Coulomb model with $m,\hbar>0$, spin zero, $\kappa>0$, $\gamma=2m\kappa/\hbar^{2}$, $c=\hbar^{2}/(2m)$, $\ell_\star>0$, $t_{\star}=2m\ell_\star^2/\hbar$, the operators $H_{\kappa}=c(-\Delta_{w}-\gamma/|\cdot|)$ and $H^{\mathrm{free}}=c(-\Delta_{w})$ on $W^{2,2}$, the comparison $U_{D}(t)$ and the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **Dollard integrable remainder.** Assume Countable Choice. For $\gamma>0$, with $H_{0}=-\Delta$, $H_{\gamma}=-\Delta-\gamma/|\cdot|$ on $H^{2}$ and the Dollard-modified evolution $U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)=e^{-i\tau H_{0}}e^{i\operatorname{sign}(\tau)a(P)\log|\tau|}$, $a(p)=\gamma/(2|p|)$, the family is unitary and the remainder $\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|\tau||P|)$ is integrable along $U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}$: there are $T_{\psi},C_{\psi}$ with $\|\bigl[\gamma/|\cdot|-\gamma/(2|\tau||P|)\bigr]U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)\psi\|_{2}\le C_{\psi}(1+\log|\tau|)/|\tau|^{2}$ for $|\tau|\ge T_{\psi}$, for vectors in the dense momentum-test class ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-integrable-remainder]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F2] **Dollard channel completeness.** With the hypotheses of [F1], the modified wave operators $\Omega_{D\pm}=s\text{-}\lim_{\tau\to\pm\infty}e^{i\tau H_{\gamma}}U_{D}^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)$ exist on all of $L^{2}$, satisfy $\Omega_{D\pm}e^{-isH_{0}}=e^{-isH_{\gamma}}\Omega_{D\pm}$, act in each angular channel as multiplication by a bounded Borel function of the energy with $|b_{l,\pm}(E)|=1$ for a.e. $E>0$, and $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_{\gamma})=H_{\mathrm c}(H_{\gamma})$; $S_{D}=\Omega_{D+}^{*}\Omega_{D-}$ is unitary ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-dollard-channel-completeness]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F3] **Spectral correspondence of a positive multiple.** For a self-adjoint operator $T$, positive $c_{0}$ and every Borel $B$, the projection valued measure of $c_{0}T$ satisfies $E_{c_{0}T}(B)=E_{T}(B/c_{0})$, so $H_{\mathrm{ac}}$, $H_{\mathrm{sc}}$, $H_{\mathrm{pp}}$ and $H_{\mathrm c}$ of $c_{0}T$ and $T$ coincide; consequently for a bounded Borel $f$ one has $f(c_{0}T)=(f\circ c_{0})(T)$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]], [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]], [[thm-unbounded-borel-functional-calculus]] clause 2, [[lem-nrqm-potentials-positive-scaling-of-self-adjoint-operators]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F4] **The model's readings.** The declared comparison, modified wave operators and spectral vocabulary are those of clauses (b), (c) of the Coulomb definition; the Coulomb operator is self-adjoint on $H^{2}$ with the flow $e^{-itH_{\kappa}/\hbar}$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] clauses (b), (c), [[pthm-nrqm-central-coulomb-energy-observable-and-flow]] clauses (a), (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; represent the physical data numerically in SI, compare with the supplied mathematical Dollard evolution through a fixed incoming or outgoing energy phase, and transfer the full limits, intertwining, completeness and scattering unitarity.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Numerical SI comparison with dimensionless arguments] Write the fixed SI units as $L_0=1\,\mathrm m$, $T_0=1\,\mathrm s$, $M_0=1\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$. Let $m_0=m/M_0$, $h_0=\hbar/(E_0T_0)$, $k_0=\kappa/(E_0L_0)$, $L=\ell_\star/L_0>0$ and $t_0=t/T_0$ be their numerical values, and put $\gamma_0=\gamma L_0=2m_0k_0/h_0^2$, $c_0=h_0^2/(2m_0)$ and $\tau=h_0t_0/(2m_0)$. These are pure real numbers, with $\tau\to\pm\infty$ as $t\to\pm\infty$. Represent the wavefunctions in the numerical SI coordinate $q=x/L_0$, with the normalized $L^2$ coordinate map $\mathcal J_0f(q)=L_0^{3/2}f(L_0q)$, the Jacobian normalization understood in the chosen length unit. Substitution in the integral proves this map unitary; weak derivative substitution gives its exact $H^2$ domain transport. The numerical energy representatives are therefore $\mathsf H_\kappa=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H_\kappa\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0C_{\gamma_0}$ and $\mathsf H_f=E_0^{-1}\mathcal J_0H^{\mathrm{free}}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=c_0A_0$, where $A_0=-\Delta_q$ and $C_{\gamma_0}=-\Delta_q-\gamma_0/|q|$. Thus $\mathcal J_0e^{-itH_\kappa/\hbar}\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}$ and similarly for the free operator. The numerical reference time is $t_{\star,0}=2m_0L^2/h_0$, so $\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\frac{|t_0|}{t_{\star,0}}=\frac{|\tau|}{L^2},\qquad \log\frac{|t|}{t_\star}=\log|\tau|-2\log L.$ Every logarithm has a dimensionless argument; no time having units of length squared is placed inside the source logarithm. [F3, F4, given, algebra]

2.1 [Exact fixed energy phases] For a positive numerical energy $e=c_0\lambda$, the phase coefficient of the physical definition is $m_0k_0/(h_0\sqrt{2m_0e})=\gamma_0/(2\sqrt\lambda)$. By [F1], $a(P)=\gamma_0/(2|P|)$ for the numerical source $A_0=|P|^2$. For $\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}$ define the fixed bounded unitary $B_{\sigma,L}=b_{\sigma,L}(A_0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(\lambda)=\exp\Bigl(-2i\sigma\frac{\gamma_0}{2\sqrt\lambda}\log L\Bigr)\quad(\lambda>0),\qquad b_{\sigma,L}(0)=1.$ The functions are bounded unimodular Borel functions despite their oscillation near zero, so their calculus is defined on all $L^2$ and they commute with $e^{-irA_0}$ for every $r$. Spectral correspondence [F3] and step 1.1 give, for $|\tau|\ge1$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}t$, $\mathcal J_0U_D(t)\mathcal J_0^{-1}=e^{-i\tau A_0}e^{i\sigma a(P)\log|\tau|}B_{\sigma,L}=U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\sigma,L}.$ The bounded functional calculus also transports under $\mathcal J_0$: conjugating the PVM gives a regular PVM representing the numerical operator, so spectral uniqueness identifies it and simple-function approximation gives the claimed calculus transport. If desired, the annular smooth momentum class in [F1] is preserved by each $B_{\sigma,L}$ because its multiplier is smooth on every compact annulus; hence the source remainder estimate remains integrable on that class after this fixed phase. The comparison for finite $|\tau|<1$ need not equal the source's short-time extension and is irrelevant to the two asymptotic limits. [step 1.1, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

3.1 [Strong limits, isometry and intertwining] Apply [F2] at the positive numerical coupling $\gamma_0$. Let $W_\pm$ be its two full-space Dollard wave operators. Step 2.1 makes the physical comparison product, conjugated by $\mathcal J_0$, equal $e^{i\tau C_{\gamma_0}}U_D^{\mathrm{nd}}(\tau)B_{\pm,L}$ on the corresponding exterior half-line. The fixed bounded right factor and the positive scalar time change let the strong limits pass on every vector, giving $\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}W_\pm B_{\pm,L}\mathcal J_0.$ Both $W_\pm$ are isometries by [F2] and both $B_{\pm,L}$ are unitaries, so these operators are isometries. For physical $s\in\mathbb R$, put $r=h_0(s/T_0)/(2m_0)$. The numerical free/Coulomb flows are $e^{-irA_0}$ and $e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$ by step 1.1. Since $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with the free flow and $W_\pm e^{-irA_0}=e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_\pm$, conjugating gives the exact intertwining of (a). No new source existence or momentum-domain assumption was introduced. [step 1.1, step 2.1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Full completeness under the reference convention] Because $B_{\pm,L}$ are onto, step 3.1 gives $\operatorname{ran}\Omega_{D\pm}=\mathcal J_0^{-1}\operatorname{ran}W_\pm$. By [F2], this is $\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm{ac}}(C_{\gamma_0})=\mathcal J_0^{-1}H_{\mathrm c}(C_{\gamma_0})$. Positive energy scaling by $c_0$ preserves these spectral subspaces [F3], and the unitary numerical coordinate representation transports the spectral measures and their subspaces as in step 2.1. The resulting physical subspaces are exactly $H_{\mathrm{ac}}(H_\kappa)=H_{\mathrm c}(H_\kappa)$. This proves (b) for every declared reference length, preserving the source's whole continuous subspace and all angular channels. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Scattering phases, unitarity and free-flow commutation] Put $S^{\mathrm{nd}}=W_+^*W_-$. The formula in step 3.1 gives $S_D=\mathcal J_0^{-1}B_{+,L}^*S^{\mathrm{nd}}B_{-,L}\mathcal J_0.$ All factors are unitary by [F2] and step 2.1, so $S_D$ is unitary. The commutation with the free flow follows directly from the two intertwinings: taking the adjoint of the plus identity at time $-r$ gives $e^{-irA_0}W_+^*=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}$, hence $S^{\mathrm{nd}}e^{-irA_0}=W_+^*e^{-irC_{\gamma_0}}W_-=e^{-irA_0}S^{\mathrm{nd}}$. The fixed $B_{\pm,L}$ commute with that same flow, so their scattering product does too, and conjugating proves (c). Equivalently the common range projection from step 4.1 gives both $S_D^*S_D=I$ and $S_DS_D^*=I$. For any other reference time $t_\star'$, let $Q_\sigma=q_\sigma(H^{\mathrm{free}})$ with $q_\sigma(E)=\exp(-i\sigma\alpha(E)\log(t_\star'/t_\star))$, $\alpha(E)=m\kappa/(\hbar\sqrt{2mE})$ for $E>0$ and $q_\sigma(0)=1$. The defining phases give exactly $\Omega_{D\pm}'=\Omega_{D\pm}Q_\pm$ and $S_D'=Q_+^*S_DQ_-$. These incoming/outgoing factors are different sign conventions, not a claim that the scattering operator itself is unchanged. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2, F3, F4, algebra]

6.1 [Scope and assembly] Steps 3.1–5.1 establish all the original modified-limit, isometry, intertwining, full completeness and scattering-unitarity conclusions with their corrected dimensional convention. No step supplies the ordinary unmodified Coulomb wave limits, so (d) retains exactly that distinction. The reference length adds only a comparison convention and its fixed channel phases; it adds no hypothesis on a state or on the Coulomb interaction, no amplitude formula and no measured cross section. [F4, given, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Phases and observables.** The modified comparison is not unique: changing
  the reference time $t_{\star}$ changes asymptotic channel phases. The
  completeness equalities of (b) and the unitarity of (c) are invariant
  under that change, which is why the definition declares the reference time
  as a convention.
- **What would be needed for an amplitude.** An explicit Coulomb scattering
  amplitude, and with it any Rutherford-type cross section, would require the
  angular asymptotic analysis of the Coulomb continuum solutions and a
  further normalization statement; neither is contained in the completeness
  theorem, and the pair does not assert one.

items.title: The resonance model's phase-shift law, unitarity and channel cross section
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label $l$,
mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}\in\mathbb R$,
$\Gamma>0$, with the phase shift read modulo $\pi$ from $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$
and the channel cross-section reading $\sigma_{l}(E)$ of that definition.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Put $y:=\Gamma/2>0$.
For every real $E$ define the **auxiliary real-axis Lorentzian factor**
$$L(E):=\frac{y^2}{(E-E_r)^2+y^2}.$$
This is a mathematical extension of the positive-energy phase-shift factor;
physical phase shifts, $k(E)$ and cross sections remain defined only for $E>0$.
Then:

(a) for every $E>0$, $|S_l(E)|=1$ and
$$\delta_l(E)=-\operatorname{Arg}(E-E_r+iy)\quad(\mathrm{modulo}\ \pi),$$
where for $z=x+iy$ with $y>0$, $\operatorname{Arg}z$ is the unique angle
$\theta\in(0,\pi)$ with $\cos\theta=x/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and
$\sin\theta=y/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$. Equivalently, for $E\ne E_r$ one may use
$\delta_l(E)=-\arctan(y/(E-E_r))$ modulo $\pi$; if $E=E_r>0$,
$\delta_l(E)=-\pi/2$ modulo $\pi$;

(b) for every $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l(E)=L(E)$. On the entire real axis,
$L(E)$ has value $1$ exactly at $E=E_r$ and value $1/2$ exactly at
$E=E_r\pm\Gamma/2$. Thus the **full-real-axis half-height width** of this
factor is $\Gamma$ for every real $E_r$. A peak or half-height location is
in the physical energy range only when that location is positive; the
width statement itself concerns $L$ on $\mathbb R$;

(c) for every $E>0$, the channel cross-section reading is
$$\sigma_l(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^2}(2l+1)L(E),\qquad k(E)=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},$$
read in $\mathrm{m^2}$. If $E_r>0$, its value at that physical energy is
$$\sigma_l(E_r)=\frac{4\pi\hbar^2}{2mE_r}(2l+1).$$
If $E_r\le0$, this model defines no physical cross section at $E_r$.
No maximum statement at $E_r$ is made for $\sigma_l$ itself, whose energy
dependence also contains the factor $k(E)^{-2}$; no slow-variation
assumption on that factor is required.

Every display is a conditional algebraic statement about the declared model;
no potential producing $S_{l}$, no decay law, no lifetime and no measured
quantity is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared single-channel resonance model with channel label $l$, parameters $E_{r}$, $\Gamma>0$, the phase-shift and cross-section readings, and the choice hypotheses.

[F1] **The declared channel factor.** For $E>0$, $S_{l}(E)=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}$ and $S_{l}=e^{2i\delta_{l}}$ modulo $\pi$, with $\sigma_{l}(E)=\frac{4\pi}{k(E)^{2}}(2l+1)\sin^{2}\delta_{l}(E)$ and $k(E)=\hbar^{-1}\sqrt{2mE}$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] clause (b)).

[F2] **Resonance model algebra in the cited mathematics.** For the single-channel model $S(E)=\frac{E-E_{r}-i\Gamma/2}{E-E_{r}+i\Gamma/2}$ with $\Gamma>0$, $|S(E)|=1$ for real $E$ and $\sin^{2}\delta=(\Gamma/2)^{2}/((E-E_{r})^{2}+(\Gamma/2)^{2})$, and substituting into the phase-shift series gives the corresponding single-channel cross section ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-partial-wave-cross-section-convergence]] clause (c)).

[F3] **The pair's channel reading.** The channel cross-section reading of the pair is the summand of the phase-shift series of the partial-wave theorem, with $l$, $\delta_{l}$ and $k$ read as in the resonance model ([[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (c), [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] clause (b)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; compute $|S_{l}|$ and the phase of the declared factor, then substitute the declared function into the model's channel reading.

**Given:** the data and hypotheses of the statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 For any real $E$, write $x:=E-E_r$ and $y:=\Gamma/2>0$. Then $x+iy\ne0$ and the purely algebraic ratio $R(E):=(x-iy)/(x+iy)$ has modulus one because its numerator is the conjugate of its denominator. On the physical range $E>0$, [F1] identifies $R(E)=S_l(E)$, proving the first part of (a). Defining $R$ as an auxiliary real-axis rational formula does not assign $k$ or a physical cross section outside the range $E>0$. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 With $r:=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}>0$ and $\theta:=\operatorname{Arg}(x+iy)\in(0,\pi)$, one has $x+iy=r e^{i\theta}$ and $x-iy=r e^{-i\theta}$, hence $R(E)=e^{-2i\theta}$. For $E>0$ the phase $\delta_l=-\theta$ modulo $\pi$ therefore matches [F1]. When $x\ne0$, $\tan\theta=y/x$ and the principal arctangent gives the same angle modulo $\pi$; when $x=0$, $\theta=\pi/2$, so the phase is $-\pi/2$ with no division by zero. This proves all of (a). [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For $E>0$, $\sin^2\delta_l=\sin^2\theta=y^2/(x^2+y^2)=L(E)$, in agreement with [F2]. Independently, the real-axis formula has positive denominator for every real $E$ and satisfies $0<L(E)\le1$, with equality $L(E)=1$ exactly when $x=0$. Also $L(E)=1/2$ if and only if $x^2=y^2$, so its two real half-height points are $E_r-y$ and $E_r+y$, separated by $2y=\Gamma$. Restricting a point to the physical range requires that point to be positive; the mathematical peak and width identities impose no condition such as $E_r>y$. This proves (b). [F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For $E>0$, substituting step 3.1 into [F1], [F3] gives $\sigma_l(E)=4\pi(2l+1)L(E)/k(E)^2$. If $E_r>0$, this formula is defined at $E=E_r$, where $L(E_r)=1$ and $k(E_r)^2=2mE_r/\hbar^2$, yielding the displayed resonance-centre value. If $E_r\le0$, no such physical evaluation is in the model's domain and the auxiliary $L(E_r)=1$ does not create one. The extra factor $k(E)^{-2}$ remains energy dependent, so no location-of-maximum or slow-variation assertion is used. This proves (c), retaining every real $E_r$ and positive $\Gamma$. [F1, F3, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Why no peak claim.** The auxiliary real-axis Lorentzian factor peaks at $E_r$; that peak is physical only if $E_r>0$. The full
  channel reading carries the factor $k(E)^{-2}$ as well; the pair states the
  full-real-axis half-height width of the Lorentzian factor, which is exactly $\Gamma$,
  without asserting where the maximum of $\sigma_{l}$ lies.
- **Modulo $\pi$.** Both $\sin^{2}$ and the cross-section reading are
  insensitive to the modulo-$\pi$ ambiguity of $\delta_{l}$.

Half-height locations have a physical reading only when positive. Conditional algebra of a declared model; no producing potential, decay law, lifetime or measured width or count is asserted.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the three-dimensional scattering page
items.statement:
## Remarks

**What the page establishes, and what it does not.**

- *Model deductions.* The page proves, conditionally on the declared
  short-range model and the cited mathematics, the existence of the wave
  operators, their isometry and intertwining
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]]), the
  asymptotic completeness and unitarity of the scattering operator for the
  compact-support and resolvent-tail classes
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-compact-support-asymptotic-completeness]],
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]]), the
  stationary outgoing solution with its amplitude and the cross-section
  readings ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-stationary-wave-amplitude-and-flux]]), the controlled
  Born approximation with its operator-norm condition
  ([[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]), the phase-shift
  cross-section series, the on-shell operator identification, and the
  conditional resonance-model algebra. Every one of these is a logical
  consequence of the stated postulates, model declarations, hypotheses and
  mathematics; none of them is an observation.
- *No observations.* The page reports no experiment: it contains no apparatus,
  no calibration, no sample, no count, no uncertainty budget and no measured
  cross section. Nothing on the page should be read as a measurement of $V$,
  $\kappa$, a phase shift or a resonance parameter.
- *What a comparison would require.* To compare the model quantities
  $d\sigma/d\Omega$ or $\sigma$ with data one needs a declared target
  preparation (target density and composition), an incident fluence with its
  own uncertainty, a stated scattering geometry, a detector acceptance and
  efficiency model, and a background model, together with a declared
  statistical model for the counts. The equal-channel elastic flux assumptions
  of the beam model ([[def-nrqm-scattering-stationary-beam-and-cross-section-model]]
  clause (d)) must be justified for the particular apparatus; inelastic or
  multichannel processes lie outside the model and would require separate
  channels.
- *Interpretation.* Agreement of a measured count rate with the model reading
  is evidence for the combined model-plus-apparatus assumptions; it is not a
  deduction that the declared model, its potential class or the framework
  describes nature. Disagreement would not by itself falsify the whole
  framework, and a finite dataset can be compatible with a model without
  confirming it.

**Scope of the model declarations.** The potential is prescribed, not derived;
the Coulomb coupling $\kappa$ and the resonance parameters $E_{r},\Gamma$ are
model parameters, not measured constants; and the modified Dollard comparison
of the Coulomb model is a declared construction whose phase convention changes
only asymptotic channel phases
([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]] clauses (c), (d)).

items.title: Long-range, threshold and model-scope limits of the scattering page
items.statement:
## Remarks

- **Long-range tails.** The short-range classes of
  [[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (b) exclude the
  pure Coulomb tail: the decaying-tail criterion of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c)
  requires a positive power $\delta>0$, and the Coulomb quotient
  $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V(x)|$ is unbounded for every $\delta>0$. The general resolvent-tail exclusion follows from clause (d) of that same theorem: its translated compact-bump input gives $h(r)\ge C/(2r+R)$ with $C>0$, which is not integrable. The Coulomb
  case is treated by the modified Dollard comparison
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]]), for which the ordinary
  short-range comparison is not claimed.
- **Threshold.** The completeness statements of this page are made for the
  declared classes and do not require a zero-energy nonresonance hypothesis
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-resolvent-tail-short-range-completeness]]).
  A different uniformity statement fails at zero energy: for compactly
  supported potentials the scattering defects are not compact uniformly when
  the energy cutoff does not vanish at $0$
  ([[thm-nrqm-controlled-dynamics-compact-scattering-defects]]). The general stationary beam and amplitude theorems use $k>0$ and give no uniform zero-energy amplitude statement. The companion's declared square-well computation separately proves its explicit zero-energy resonance profile.
- **Positive eigenvalues.** The absence of positive eigenvalues is part of
  [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-wave-operator-existence-and-free-continuity]] clause
  (d) for the compact-support class; no statement is made about negative or
  zero eigenvalues of the interacting operator, and no general bound-state inventory belongs to this page. The companion's explicit well has a separately proved local threshold branch, without a bound-state count for arbitrary potentials.
- **Resonances.** The resonance model
  ([[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]]) is a declared
  conditional model; the page proves no existence of a resonance for any
  declared potential and makes no analytic-continuation claim for the
  resolvent or the scattering operator.

items.title: S-wave phase shift of a declared spherical square well, with its low-energy limit and hard-sphere comparison
items.statement:
## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **spherical square well**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}-U,&|x|<a,\\ 0,&|x|\ge a,\end{cases}\qquad U>0,\ a>0,$$
read in joules and metres; $V$ is real, bounded and compactly supported, so it
is in the compact-support class. Adopt the central stationary reading at wave
number $k>0$ of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] and the
$s$-wave ($l=0$) channel. Put
$$K:=\frac{\sqrt{2m(E+U)}}{\hbar},\qquad k:=\frac{\sqrt{2mE}}{\hbar},\qquad E>0 .$$
Because the declared potential is constant on each of the two regions and
bounded, the reduced radial function $u_0:=\varphi_0$ of the cited channel
vocabulary (up to a nonzero real normalization) is $C^1$ at $r=a$
with second derivative given by the reduced equation on each side, and the
$s$-wave phase shift is determined by matching: $u_{0}\propto\sin(Kr)$ for
$r<a$ and $u_{0}\propto\sin(kr+\delta_{0})$ for $r>a$.

The phase is read modulo $\pi$. For $z=X+iY\ne0$, $\arg z$ means an angle $\theta$ modulo $2\pi$ with $\cos\theta=X/|z|$ and $\sin\theta=Y/|z|$; hence $\arg z$ modulo $\pi$ determines the phase without dividing by $X$ or $Y$. Big-$O$ terms below are for $k\to0^+$ at a fixed depth and radius; depth comparisons are taken after that low-energy limit.

## Verification

**Given:** the data of the setup and the reduced equation of the $s$-wave of
[[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clause (b).

[F1] The actual channel supplier defines the regular function itself as the reduced radial solution, with $\varphi_0(r)/r\to1$ at the origin, the exterior outgoing function $e^{ikr}$ and the channel ratio $S_0=\overline{W(u_0,e^{ikr})}/W(u_0,e^{ikr})=e^{2i\delta_0}$. Its channel cross-section is $\sigma_0=4\pi\sin^2\delta_0/k^2$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-and-phase-shift-readings]] clauses (b),(c), [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-partial-wave-cross-section]] clauses (b),(c)).

[F2] The derivatives of sine and cosine and $\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$ are [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]] and [[cor-trigonometric-parity-and-pythagorean-identity]]. The finite Taylor remainder estimate with a locally bounded next derivative is [[cor-taylor-remainder-bound]]. The existence of a zero between opposite signs of a continuous real function is [[thm-intermediate-value]]; strict decrease follows from a negative derivative by [[cor-mean-value-theorem]].

[F3] For a radial function $f(x)=u(|x|)/|x|$, polar integration gives $\|f\|_2^2=4\pi\int_0^\infty|u(r)|^2dr$ ([[thm-polar-coordinates-formula-for-lebesgue-measure]], $n=3$, and $\sigma(S^2)=4\pi$ from [[lem-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-sphere-integral-in-angle-coordinates]] clause (b)). The weak domain $W^{2,2}$ requires square-integrable weak derivatives through order two ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]), and the declared bounded-well energy operator has that domain and acts as $-c\Delta+V$, $c=\hbar^2/(2m)$ ([[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] clause (c)).

1.1 For $r<a$ the reduced equation is $u_0''=-K^2u_0$, so its nonzero real regular solution is $u_0(r)=A\sin(Kr)$, $A\ne0$, with $u_0(0)=0$; the normalization in [F1] corresponds to $A=1/K$. For $r>a$ a nonzero real solution has the form $B\sin(kr+\delta_0)$ with real $B\ne0$. The regular solution and its derivative are absolutely continuous locally through the bounded step potential; integrating the radial equation across $a$ gives no jump of $u_0'$ or $u_0$. Thus $A\sin(Ka)=B\sin(ka+\delta_0)$ and $AK\cos(Ka)=Bk\cos(ka+\delta_0)$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Put $X:=K\cos(Ka)$, $Y:=k\sin(Ka)$ and $z:=X+iY$. Since $k,K>0$ and sine and cosine cannot both vanish, $X^2+Y^2>0$. With $\theta:=ka+\delta_0$, the matching equations give $Bk\cos\theta=AX$, $Bk\sin\theta=AY$, hence $e^{2i\theta}=z/\overline z$ regardless of the real sign of $A/B$. Consequently $S_0(k)=e^{-2ika}\,(K\cos(Ka)+ik\sin(Ka))/(K\cos(Ka)-ik\sin(Ka))$ and $\delta_0=\arg z-ka$ modulo $\pi$, with a nonzero denominator for every positive energy and depth. This is also the actual Wronskian convention of [F1], since outside the well $W(u_0,e^{ikr})=-Bk e^{-i\delta_0}$. Where $\cos(Ka)\ne0$, the equivalent local formula is $\tan(ka+\delta_0)=(k/K)\tan(Ka)$; the complex formula remains valid when either matching value vanishes. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Fix $U>0$ and put $\gamma:=\sqrt{2mU}/\hbar$, so $K=\sqrt{\gamma^2+k^2}$ and $K-\gamma=k^2/(K+\gamma)=O(k^2)$. If $\cos(\gamma a)\ne0$, choose the representative of $\theta$ tending to zero modulo $\pi$. The tangent is smooth near $\gamma a$, so $\tan\theta=(k/K)\tan(Ka)=k\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma+O(k^3)$. By [F2], $\tan\theta=\theta+O(\theta^3)$ near zero; first $\theta=O(k)$ and then $\theta=k\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma+O(k^3)$. Hence $\delta_0=-k a_{\mathrm{eff}}+O(k^3)$ modulo $\pi$, where $a_{\mathrm{eff}}:=a-\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma$, and [F1] gives $\sigma_0\to4\pi a_{\mathrm{eff}}^2$. The expansion uses locally bounded derivatives only where $\cos(\gamma a)\ne0$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 At an exact threshold $\gamma a=\alpha_n:=(n+\tfrac12)\pi$, $n\ge0$, write $s_n:=\sin\alpha_n=(-1)^n$. The identity for $K-\gamma$ and [F2] give $K-\gamma=k^2/(2\gamma)+O(k^4)$, $X=K\cos(Ka)=-s_n a k^2/2+O(k^4)$ and $Y=k\sin(Ka)=s_n k+O(k^5)$. Thus $X/Y=-ak/2+O(k^3)$ and the angle of $X+iY$ tends to $\pi/2$ modulo $\pi$. Writing $\theta=\pi/2+\varepsilon$ modulo $\pi$, $\cot\theta=-\varepsilon+O(\varepsilon^3)$ gives $\varepsilon=ak/2+O(k^3)$, so $\delta_0=\pi/2-ak/2+O(k^3)$ modulo $\pi$. Therefore $k^2\sigma_0=4\pi\sin^2\delta_0\to4\pi$; the finite-scattering-length formula of step 3.1 does not apply at this depth. At zero energy the regular reduced solution is proportional to $\sin(\gamma r)$ inside and to the nonzero constant $s_n$ outside, with matching derivative zero at $a$. Its spatial form is proportional to $1/r$ outside and is not square integrable by [F3]; this is the zero-energy s-wave resonance meant here. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

5.1 In the finite-length branch, as $\gamma a\uparrow\alpha_n$ from below, $\tan(\gamma a)\to+\infty$ and $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to-\infty$; from above $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to+\infty$. Thus the iterated low-energy reading $4\pi a_{\mathrm{eff}}^2$ diverges on either approach, while the exact-threshold law is step 4.1. Along nonresonant depth regimes with $\tan(\gamma a)/\gamma\to0$, $a_{\mathrm{eff}}\to a$ and the iterated low-energy reading tends to $4\pi a^2$, four times the geometric area $\pi a^2$. In particular at $\gamma a=n\pi$, $n\ge1$, $a_{\mathrm{eff}}=a$ and $\delta_0=-ka+O(k^3)$; the interior node tends to the boundary. This comparison holds along the stated depth regimes, rather than for every sequence of large depths. [F1, F2, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 The bound-state interpretation has a separate negative-energy proof. Write $g:=\gamma a$. For $\alpha_n<g<(n+1)\pi$, define $f_g(x):=x\cot x+\sqrt{g^2-x^2}$ on $[\alpha_n,g]$. It is continuous, $f_g(\alpha_n)=\sqrt{g^2-\alpha_n^2}>0$ and $f_g(g)=g\cot g<0$; [F2] gives a root $x_g\in(\alpha_n,g)$. On that open interval $f_g'=\cot x-x\csc^2x-x/\sqrt{g^2-x^2}<0$, so the root is unique. Put $q:=x_g/a$, $\kappa:=\sqrt{g^2-x_g^2}/a>0$ and $u(r):=\sin(qr)$ for $r\le a$, $u(r):=\sin(qa)e^{-\kappa(r-a)}$ for $r\ge a$. Then $q^2+\kappa^2=\gamma^2$ and $q\cot(qa)=-\kappa$, so both $u$ and $u'$ match at $a$. The spatial function $\psi(x):=u(|x|)/|x|$, with value $q$ at zero, is nonzero and square integrable by [F3]; it is smooth near zero, decays exponentially at infinity and is piecewise smooth with matching first derivatives at $a$. Its weak derivatives through order two are square integrable, with no boundary delta term, hence $\psi\in W^{2,2}$. The radial identity $\Delta(u(r)/r)=u''(r)/r$ for $r>0$ gives $H\psi=-c\kappa^2\psi$, $c=\hbar^2/(2m)$, so normalization produces a genuine s-wave bound eigenvector. As $g\downarrow\alpha_n$, $0<\kappa a\le\sqrt{g^2-\alpha_n^2}\to0$, while for $g\le\alpha_n$ there is no matching root in this branch $x>\alpha_n$ with $x\le g$. Thus a new negative-energy s-wave branch appears just above each stated threshold, whose endpoint is the non-square-integrable zero-energy resonance in step 4.1; no assertion about other angular channels or the full bound-state count is needed. [F2, F3, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 For the free consistency case $U=0$, $K=k$ and step 2.1 gives $S_0=e^{-2ika}(\cos ka+i\sin ka)/(\cos ka-i\sin ka)=1$, so $\delta_0=0$ modulo $\pi$ at every positive energy, including zeros of sine or cosine. At any positive-depth energy with $Ka=n\pi$, $n\ge1$, one has $Y=0$ and $X\ne0$, hence $S_0=e^{-2ika}$ and $\delta_0=-ka$ modulo $\pi$: this is exactly the exterior phase for the vanishing radial boundary condition of a hard sphere at that energy. If $\cos(Ka)=0$, the same formula gives $S_0=-e^{-2ika}$ and $\delta_0=\pi/2-ka$ modulo $\pi$. These checks complete the full positive-energy, zero-depth and matching-node cases together with the two low-energy branches above. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 5.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is asserted.** The phase shift, both low-energy branches, the locally proved s-wave bound-state threshold and the
  hard-sphere comparison are exact consequences of the declared well and the
  channel vocabulary; no measured phase shift or cross section is reported,
  and no claim is made that the spherical square well describes any material
  target.
- **Idealisation.** The well is an idealised declared potential: it is
  discontinuous at $|x|=a$, and the depth comparisons of steps 4.1 and 5.1
  are limits inside the declared family of wells ($K_{0}a\to(n+\frac12)\pi$
  or $\tan(K_{0}a)/K_{0}\to0$), not limits of a measured potential.

items.title: The declared single-channel resonance: Lorentzian factor, half-height points and resonance-value cross section
items.statement:
## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared single-channel resonance model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-model]] with channel label
$l=0$, mass $m>0$, action constant $\hbar>0$ and parameters $E_{r}>0$,
$\Gamma>0$; read the phase shift and channel cross section by
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]] clauses (a)-(c).
Put $k_r:=k(E_r)=\hbar^{-1}\sqrt{2mE_r}$ and let $L(E)$ on
$\mathbb R$ denote the auxiliary Lorentzian factor of that theorem.

## Verification

**Given:** the declared model data and the statements of
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]].

1.1 Since $E_r>0$, the theorem can be evaluated at the physical energy $E_r$, giving $\sin^2\delta_0(E_r)=L(E_r)=1$ and $\sigma_0(E_r)=4\pi/k_r^2=4\pi\hbar^2/(2mE_r)$ in $\mathrm{m^2}$. The real-axis factor has $L(E_r\pm\Gamma/2)=1/2$. The upper point is always positive; the lower point is positive exactly if $\Gamma<2E_r$, equals the excluded boundary $0$ if $\Gamma=2E_r$, and is negative if $\Gamma>2E_r$. Only positive points have physical phase and cross-section readings. [given, algebra]

2.1 For every physical $E>0$, with $x:=E-E_r$ and $y:=\Gamma/2>0$, dividing by the positive resonance-centre value yields $\sigma_0(E)/\sigma_0(E_r)=(k_r/k(E))^2 y^2/(x^2+y^2)=(E_r/E)L(E)$. At the always-positive upper point the ratio is $E_r/(2(E_r+y))$; at the lower point it is $E_r/(2(E_r-y))$ only when $E_r-y>0$. If that lower point is zero or negative, the real-axis identity $L(E_r-y)=1/2$ is still valid but no physical ratio is evaluated there. The factor $E_r/E$ is energy dependent and need not vary slowly for arbitrary $\Gamma$. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Take the declared parameters $E_{r}=4\,\Gamma$ (both in joules). Then at $E=E_{r}+\Gamma/2=(9/2)\Gamma$ the Lorentzian factor is $1/2$ and the ratio of step 2.1 is $(4/(9/2))(1/2)=4/9$; at $E=(7/2)\Gamma$ the factor is again $1/2$ and the ratio is $(4/(7/2))(1/2)=4/7$. The first value is strictly below $1/2$ and the second strictly above, so this is the explicit asymmetry produced by the $1/E$ factor, so these factor half-height locations are not the locations where $\sigma_0(E)=\sigma_0(E_r)/2$; no maximum of $\sigma_0$ is used in this comparison. [step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 On the full real axis, $L$ reaches $1$ at $E_r$ and $1/2$ exactly at $E_r\pm\Gamma/2$, so its full width at half maximum is $\Gamma$. On the positive physical axis both half-height locations are present exactly when $\Gamma<2E_r$; for $\Gamma\ge2E_r$ the lower location is excluded. This qualifies the physical interpretation without narrowing the allowed $E_r>0$, $\Gamma>0$ parameters or changing the real-axis width identity. The example of step 3.1 keeps both half-height points positive and shows that the cross-section ratios there differ from $1/2$. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **No decay claim.** The width parameter $\Gamma$ is an energy parameter of
  the declared factor; the pair does not identify $\hbar/\Gamma$ with a
  lifetime and does not derive an exponential decay law.
- **No maximum claim.** Because of the factor $1/E$ in the ratio computed in
  step 2.1, the pair makes no statement that $\sigma_{0}$ attains its maximum
  at $E_{r}$; only the auxiliary Lorentzian factor's full-real-axis half-height width is asserted, with positive-energy locations qualified above.

Conditional algebra only; no producing potential, decay law or measured width or count is asserted.

items.title: Born amplitude of a declared uniform ball potential with an explicit weak-coupling condition
items.statement:
## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$ and the **uniform ball potential**
$$V(x):=\begin{cases}V_{0},&|x|<R,\\ 0,&|x|>R,\end{cases}\qquad V_{0}\in\mathbb R,\ R>0,$$
read in joules and metres; adopt the stationary beam model at wave number
$k>0$ and direction $d$, and let $W=(2m/\hbar^{2})V$, $q=\|K_{k}\|$, $f_{k}$
and the Born amplitude $f_{B}$ be as in
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-controlled-born-approximation]]. Write
$\theta$ for the scattering angle, $\cos\theta=\Omega\cdot d$, and
$\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=k(d-\Omega)$ for the wave-vector transfer and $q_{\mathrm{tr}}:=|\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}|=2k\sin(\theta/2)$ for its magnitude.

## Verification

**Given:** the declared model data, the Born theorem of the pair, and the polar-coordinates formula for Lebesgue measure.

1.1 By the Born theorem, $f_{B}(\Omega)=-\frac{1}{4\pi}\int_{B_{R}}e^{i\mathbf q_{\mathrm{tr}}\cdot y}W(y)\,dy$ with $W=V_{0}2m/\hbar^{2}$ constant on $B_{R}$; in polar coordinates the ball integral is $\int_{B_{R}}e^{iq\cdot y}dy=2\pi\int_{0}^{R}\int_{-1}^{1}e^{iqrs}r^{2}\,ds\,dr=4\pi\bigl(\sin(qR)-qR\cos(qR)\bigr)/q^{3}$ for $q=q_{\mathrm{tr}}>0$, and equals $4\pi R^{3}/3$ at $q=0$ by continuity. [given, algebra]

1.2 The kernel $G_{k}(x-y)W(y)$ on $B_{R}\times B_{R}$ has squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm $\int_{B_{R}}\int_{B_{R}}|G_{k}(x-y)W(y)|^{2}dx\,dy=\frac{|V_{0}|^{2}(2m/\hbar^{2})^{2}}{16\pi^{2}}\int_{B_{R}}\int_{B_{R}}|x-y|^{-2}dx\,dy$; for each $y$ the inner integral over $x\in B_{R}$ is at most the integral over the ball of radius $2R$ around $y$, which is $8\pi R$. Hence $\|K_{k}\|\le\|K_{k}\|_{\mathrm{HS}}\le\frac{2m|V_{0}|}{\hbar^{2}}R^{2}\sqrt{2/3}=:q_{\mathrm{HS}}$. [given, algebra]

2.1 Therefore $f_{B}(\Omega)=-\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\cdot\frac{\sin(q_{\mathrm{tr}}R)-q_{\mathrm{tr}}R\cos(q_{\mathrm{tr}}R)}{q_{\mathrm{tr}}^{3}}$ for $q_{\mathrm{tr}}>0$, with the forward value $f_{B}(\theta=0)=-\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\frac{R^{3}}{3}$; the amplitude has the dimension of length, since $2mV_{0}/\hbar^{2}$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$ and the bracket in $\mathrm{m^{3}}$. [step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 Consequently, if $\frac{2m|V_{0}|}{\hbar^{2}}R^{2}\sqrt{2/3}<1$, then $q=\|K_{k}\|\le q_{\mathrm{HS}}<1$ and the controlled Born estimate of the theorem applies; since $t\mapsto t/(1-t)$ is increasing on $[0,1)$ and $\|e_{\mathrm{inc}}\|_{L^{2}(B_{R})}=|B_{R}|^{1/2}$, the uniform error bound is at most $|f_{k}(\Omega)-f_{B}(\Omega)|\le\frac{\|W\|_{\infty}|B_{R}|}{4\pi}\frac{q_{\mathrm{HS}}}{1-q_{\mathrm{HS}}}=\frac{2m|V_{0}|}{\hbar^{2}}\frac{R^{3}}{3}\frac{q_{\mathrm{HS}}}{1-q_{\mathrm{HS}}}$ in metres; this is an explicit condition on the declared strength, radius, mass and action constant, verified here without any numerical value of the constants. [step 1.2, given, algebra]

3.1 Under the same condition the beam model reads $d\sigma/d\Omega(0)=|f_{k}(0)|^{2}$, and the theorem controls the difference from $|f_{B}(0)|^{2}$ through the bound of 2.2; the pair asserts the display $|f_{B}(0)|^{2}=\bigl(\frac{2mV_{0}}{\hbar^{2}}\bigr)^{2}\frac{R^{6}}{9}$ as the Born forward reading, read in $\mathrm{m^{2}\,sr^{-1}}$, and no measured value. [step 2.1, step 2.2, given, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **Scope.** The Born amplitude is a conditional model quantity; the explicit
  condition of 2.2 is sufficient for the controlled error bound of the pair
  and is not claimed to be necessary.
- **No weak-potential language.** The pair avoids "for a weak potential";
  the condition is the operator-norm condition $q<1$, verified here through
  the displayed Hilbert-Schmidt bound.

items.title: A Yukawa tail satisfies the resolvent-tail class while the Coulomb limit does not
items.statement:
## Example

**Setup.** Adopt the declared short-range scattering model
[[def-nrqm-scattering-framework-short-range-model]] with mass $m>0$, spin
zero, action constant $\hbar>0$, and declare the **Yukawa potential**
$$V_{g,\mu}(x):=-g\,\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}\qquad(x\ne0),\qquad g>0,\ \mu>0,$$
read in joules, with $g$ in $\mathrm{J\,m}$ and $\mu$ in $\mathrm{m^{-1}}$.

## Verification

**Given:** the declared model data and the hypotheses of
[[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clauses (c), (d).

1.1 Put $V_{\mathrm{loc}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|<1\}}$ and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}:=V_{g,\mu}\mathbf 1_{\{|x|\ge1\}}$, so that $V_{g,\mu}=V_{\mathrm{loc}}+V_{\mathrm{tail}}$; $V_{\mathrm{loc}}$ is supported in the closed unit ball, and $\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}|V_{\mathrm{loc}}|^{2}dx=4\pi g^{2}\int_{0}^{1}e^{-2\mu r}dr\le4\pi g^{2}<\infty$, so $V_{\mathrm{loc}}\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3})$ is compactly supported and $V_{\mathrm{tail}}$ is bounded by $g$. [given, algebra]

2.1 For $|x|\ge1$ one has $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|=g\,e^{-\mu|x|}/|x|\le g\,e^{-\mu|x|}$, and for every $\delta>0$ the function $r\mapsto e^{-\mu r}(1+r)^{1+\delta}$ is bounded on $[0,\infty)$: on a compact initial interval it is continuous hence bounded, and beyond some $R_{0}$ the estimate $e^{\mu r}\ge C(1+r)^{\delta+1}$ of the cited dominance theorem gives $e^{-\mu r}(1+r)^{1+\delta}\le C^{-1}$; hence with the constant $C_{\delta}:=\sup_{r\ge0}e^{-\mu r}(1+r)^{1+\delta}<\infty$ one has $|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|\le gC_{\delta}(1+|x|)^{-1-\delta}$ for all $|x|\ge1$, and a fortiori almost everywhere on $\mathbb R^{3}$ after adjusting the constant, since the region $|x|<1$ is anyway covered by the local part. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 By 1.1 and 2.1 the declared Yukawa potential has the decaying-tail form of [[pthm-nrqm-scattering-resolvent-tail-asymptotic-completeness]] clause (c) with any $\delta>0$; hence, by that theorem, the model's interacting operator is self-adjoint on $W^{2,2}$, its wave operators exist and are asymptotically complete with vanishing singular continuous spectrum, and its scattering operator is unitary. [step 2.1, given, algebra]

4.1 As $\mu\to0^{+}$ the potential $V_{g,\mu}$ tends pointwise to $-g/|x|$, the pure Coulomb form with $\kappa=g$; for the limiting potential, and for every split into a compactly supported part and a remainder, the quotient $(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}|V_{\mathrm{tail}}(x)|=g(1+|x|)^{1+\delta}/|x|$ tends to $+\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$ for every $\delta>0$, so the sufficient decay hypothesis of that theorem fails and the Coulomb case is not covered by the short-range class; its treatment is the separate declared long-range model [[def-nrqm-scattering-coulomb-dollard-model]], for which the theorem supplies no ordinary-comparison statement. [step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What is checked.** The example verifies the class hypothesis for the
  screened potential through explicit integrability and boundedness, and it
  verifies the failure of the sufficient decay hypothesis in the unscreened
  limit; it asserts nothing about the actual size of the resolvent tail
  function $h(r)$ for the Yukawa potential beyond the class membership.
- **No measured screening.** The screening parameter $\mu$ is a declared
  model parameter, not a measured inverse length, and the limit $\mu\to0^{+}$
  is a limit inside the declared family of models.

references.title: R. Fitzpatrick, Quantum Mechanics (University of Texas at Austin, author-hosted course text), Section 15.4 printed pages 214-215: the Yukawa potential reducing to the Coulomb potential as the screening parameter tends to zero
J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 12.4 printed pages 271-275 (PDF pages 279-283): scattering off hydrogen with a shielded Coulomb potential

  [[ex-nrqm-scattering-single-channel-resonance-cross-section]], the uniform

  uncertainty budget on this page, and no number appearing here is a measured

- **Symbolic parameters.** The depth and radius of the well, the resonance

  screening parameter remain symbolic throughout; the examples verify
  identities and class memberships, and assert no numerical value of $m$ or
  $\hbar$.
- **No extrapolation.** The hard-sphere comparison of the square-well example
  is a limit inside the declared family of wells; the low-energy limit is
  taken for the exact phase shift of the declared well and is not asserted as
  a universal low-energy law. The failures and limits recorded in the Yukawa
  example are statements about the declared potential class, not about any
